findings.problem: Light mode removes the teal brand language and leaves the wireframe room in low-contrast grey, making it feel like an unrelated default theme.
findings.fix: Define a light-mode teal accent and stronger two-tier wireframe strokes while retaining restrained light surfaces.

findings.problem: At this display scale the top-bar data and dock controls are materially smaller than in c01, reducing glanceability and hit-target confidence.
findings.fix: Set minimum logical sizing for panel text, indicators, icons, and dock targets so HiDPI/scaling changes do not shrink the primary controls.

findings.location: Overview workspace strip and window previews
findings.problem: The overview shows one oversized mostly empty workspace card, a clipped adjacent card, and tiny window previews, so switching workspaces or windows is not scannable.
findings.fix: Use the available canvas to size and center workspace thumbnails consistently, expose multiple workspaces intentionally, and make active-window previews readable.

findings.problem: The application grid is extremely sparse, while two small duplicate room thumbnails consume the strongest visual position without communicating a useful overview state.
findings.fix: Use a denser, consistent app-grid layout and either remove the redundant thumbnails or turn them into legible workspace/window previews.

findings.problem: The panel’s bright teal selected controls compete with the wallpaper accent and the small utility glyphs at the top have weak discoverability.
findings.fix: Reserve saturated teal for active state indicators, add clearer labels/tooltips for header actions, and reduce emphasis on non-primary selected tiles.

findings.problem: Multiple notification titles and bodies are visibly stacked on top of each other, making every notification unreadable.
findings.fix: Constrain notifications to discrete cards with fixed vertical stacking, clipping, and overflow handling; never permit text layers to overlap.

findings.problem: The drawer covers the focal wireframe room and starts near screen center, producing a large visual obstruction rather than an edge-anchored transient panel.
findings.fix: Anchor the drawer to the top bar edge with predictable width and preserve a clearer desktop context behind it.

findings.problem: The lock screen leaves system-action icons floating in the corner without a containing panel or labels, which weakens their affordance and makes the screen feel unfinished.
findings.fix: Group the permitted lock-screen actions into a compact, consistently styled status cluster or menu with adequate targets.

findings.problem: The password field’s caret, eye icon, and oversized submit chevron are visually unbalanced, and the field has no explicit input label or error/help state.
findings.fix: Normalize the icon scale, add a persistent accessible password label or clear prompt, and specify visible validation and disabled/submitting states.

findings.location: Notification list in the calendar popover
findings.problem: Two notifications are drawn on top of each other. The 'System / Connected / Wired connection established' text overlaps 'System / Disk almost full'. Both are unreadable. The close and expand buttons also collide.
findings.fix: Fix the notification stack layout so each message gets its own row with a fixed height and spacing. Collapse stacked groups with a count instead of overlapping them.

findings.location: Banner toast at top left, behind the popover
findings.problem: The 'Backup finished' toast is clipped by the popover and overlaps it, so its text is cut off ('copied t'). Banners and the message tray fight for the same space.
findings.fix: Anchor banners at top centre and hide them while the date menu is open. Alternatively, stack the popover above the banner with a z-order that never clips text.

findings.location: Vitals items in the top bar
findings.problem: The Vitals values show '00 00 00' with no units. They look like a broken state, and nothing says which number is memory, load or network.
findings.fix: Show a real placeholder such as '–' or a skeleton until data arrives. Always show units (%, load, KB/s) and keep a fixed width.

findings.problem: The Vitals readouts (45%, 0.8, 33 KB/s) have no visual separation or hierarchy. The icons are tiny and the group runs straight into the clock. The text width changes with the value, so the bar jitters. The right-hand glyph row (clipboard, layout, screen, volume, lock/user, power) is not labelled. Several icons look alike and have unclear meanings.
findings.fix: Use tabular figures and a fixed width for each readout. Group the clock, Vitals and system icons with consistent gaps. Drop the non-essential icons or consolidate them into the quick settings.

findings.problem: The wireframe room is placed centrally and its lines are bright teal. It is the loudest object on the desktop and competes with windows and the dock. It does not feel calm at rest.
findings.fix: Lower the line opacity and glow so it sits at the background level. Offset the room so it does not sit under where windows open.

findings.location: Light mode top bar and dock
findings.problem: The top bar and dock stay dark navy on a light wallpaper. The panel does not follow the light theme. The dark pill with the Vitals feels heavy next to the pale wallpaper. The clipboard and layout icon order differs from c01 (swapped).
findings.fix: Decide whether the shell stays dark by design, and say so. Otherwise give the panel and dock a light variant. Keep the right-hand icon order the same in every mode.

findings.problem: The grey wireframe on a pale blue-grey ground has low contrast and loses the teal brand identity in light mode.
findings.fix: Give the light wallpaper a teal accent line at the same weight as the dark one.

findings.location: Top bar and dock at a smaller scale
findings.problem: At the smaller scale the top bar is much thinner (about 30px against 42px). The text and icons are tiny. The dock shrinks and its icons are closer together. Bar height, icon size and dock size do not scale with the display.
findings.fix: Define the bar and dock sizes in scale-independent units. Keep a minimum text size of about 13px at the smaller scale and keep the proportions between c01 and c03.

findings.problem: The overview shows one big workspace card holding the wallpaper and no windows. A second workspace peeks in at the right edge. The black ground behind the card is a different colour from the navy desktop. The top bar loses its pill and floats.
findings.fix: Use the same background colour as the desktop. Show window thumbnails or an empty-state hint. Keep the top bar treatment the same as on the desktop.

findings.problem: The search field is low contrast against the black ground. The placeholder text is dim grey.
findings.fix: Raise the field's fill and its text contrast, and give it a teal focus ring when active.

findings.problem: Two tiny workspace thumbnails with different sizes and heights sit between the search field and the grid. They are cropped and unaligned. The grid sits far below, with a big empty area under the last row.
findings.fix: Make the thumbnails the same size, aligned and labelled. Tighten the vertical rhythm between the search field, the strip and the grid.

findings.problem: The icons are inconsistent: Chrome, 1Password, Weather, Maps, Music and the others are in different styles. The Tela-fork icons (Construct, Install, Ptyxis) don't match the third-party ones. Labels are truncated ('Google Chr...', 'Install Con...'). Folders (Utilities, System) look different from the app tiles.
findings.fix: Normalise icon shapes and colours as far as the brand allows. Use full or two-line labels. Give the folders a clear style that matches the app tiles.

findings.problem: Toggle states are hard to tell apart. 'Wired' and 'Dark Style' are active in teal, but the fills are barely different from the inactive tiles. 'Power Mode' has a subtitle, but the others don't. There is only a volume slider, with no brightness. The icons on the top row are small and unlabelled.
findings.fix: Make the active state a solid teal fill with dark text, and keep the inactive tiles neutral. Put a subtitle on every tile or on none. Add a brightness slider. Add tooltips to the top row.

findings.problem: The highlight on the active quick settings button is a small box around four icons. It does not clearly show which control the popover belongs to.
findings.fix: Anchor the panel under the highlighted pill and round the highlight to match the pill.

findings.problem: The left half is a large empty panel for 'No Notifications', and the calendar sits cramped on the right. The calendar uses zero-padded numbers ('01', '05') and the columns are loose. The 'Clear' button is dim, so it looks disabled. The two lower buttons (Add World Clocks, Select Weather Location) are low contrast.
findings.fix: Use a plain numeral style for the days. Rebalance the two halves. Hide 'Clear' when there is nothing to clear. Bring the secondary actions up to a readable contrast.

findings.problem: The today marker is a dim teal circle with a teal numeral. It is low contrast. The month header is weaker than the 'Monday October 5 2026' header, so the hierarchy is odd.
findings.fix: Fill today with the solid accent and a dark numeral. Make the month title the same weight as the other headers.

findings.problem: The lock screen has no wireframe room and no brand. It is a black gradient with a large clock. The top bar icons (network, volume, user, power) float in the corner with no labels. There is no hint on how to unlock, for example 'swipe up'.
findings.fix: Bring the wireframe room back at low opacity. Add an unlock hint. Keep the clock but give the date a stronger weight and spacing.

findings.problem: The user avatar is a generic grey placeholder. The password field is a bare pill with no label or placeholder. The submit chevron is large and grey and sits next to a tiny eye icon, which is crowded. The teal focus ring is the only brand cue.
findings.fix: Add a 'Password' placeholder. Make the submit arrow a filled teal circle. Space the eye icon and the arrow apart. Add the CONSTRUCT mark above the avatar.

findings.problem: The dock has no running or active indicators and no labels. The icons are a mix of teal Tela-fork icons and colourful third-party ones (VS Code blue, calendar red and white). The calendar icon says FRIDAY 7 while the clock says Oct 4 or 5, which is a different date.
findings.fix: Add running dots and a focus state. Theme the third-party icons or use a coherent set. Make the calendar icon show the real date.

findings.problem: The clock shows 'Oct 4' in c01 and 'Oct 5' elsewhere, and the dock calendar says 7. The data is inconsistent across screens.
findings.fix: Use one fixed date in the captures, and make the dock icon follow the system date.

findings.location: Message tray, notification list (left column of the date menu)
findings.problem: Two notifications ('Connected / Wired connection established' and 'Disk almost full / Only 2.1 GB…') are drawn on top of each other at the same y, so both titles and bodies are illegible. A third empty card sits below them as a sliver.
findings.fix: Fix the notification list layout so each message gets its own row with an 8px gap: the stacked or collapsed group must expand into separate rows when the tray is open, or show only the top card plus a '+1' count. Never overlay text.

findings.problem: The incoming banner opens to the left of the date menu and is cut off by it: '312 files were copied t…' runs under the popover. The banner and the tray also compete at the same time.
findings.fix: Queue banners while the date menu is open, or send them straight into the tray. Otherwise put the banner under the clock with a higher z-order than the popover.

findings.location: Top bar, Vitals cluster (CPU / load / network)
findings.problem: With the date menu open, all three Vitals readouts change to '00 00 00', which looks like a broken sensor. The same happens in c08. In c01 to c06 they show real values (45%, 0.8, 33 KB/s).
findings.fix: Keep the last value when the shell stops polling under a popover. Never render the zero-padded placeholder: show '–' if no value is available yet.

findings.problem: The calendar launcher shows a static 'FRIDAY 7', but the top bar says Oct 4/Oct 5 and the date menu says Monday October 5. A stale date in the dock contradicts the clock on every screen.
findings.fix: Use a dynamic calendar icon that renders today's weekday and date, or a dateless glyph from the Tela fork.

findings.location: Top bar, right cluster between network rate and system indicators
findings.problem: The order of the clipboard and tiling-layout icons swaps between screens: clipboard then layout in c01, c04 to c08; layout then clipboard in c02 and c03. These are also full-colour or filled glyphs among outline Vitals icons, and three unlabelled square glyphs (display, boxed lock-like icon, power) sit next to each other with no grouping.
findings.fix: Pin the extension order in the panel config. Draw clipboard and layout glyphs in the same 1.5px outline symbolic style as the system icons. Put an 8–12px gap between the extension group and the quick settings group so the quick settings pill reads as one target.

findings.location: Top bar and dock in light style
findings.problem: In light mode the top bar and dock stay near-black slabs on a pale grey wallpaper, which is the heaviest contrast on screen. The wireframe also turns neutral grey, so the teal brand accent is missing from the light desktop.
findings.fix: Give light mode a light panel and dock surface (for example #F4F6F8 with a 1px #0002 border and dark text). Draw the light wallpaper's room in a darker teal (around #0E7C86) instead of grey.

findings.problem: The grid mixes three icon languages: the Tela-fork flat circles (Weather, Music, Settings), vendor icons (Chrome, 1Password, Vim with an italic wordmark) and Adwaita-style ones (Characters, Text Editor, Camera). Folder previews (Utilities, System) render as dark tiles while app icons have no tile, and Construct and 'Install Con…' use the same glyph.
findings.fix: Extend the Tela fork to cover installed vendor apps, or apply a consistent shape mask. Give the installer its own glyph, for example the room with a down arrow. Make folder tiles match the icon footprint.

findings.problem: 'Google Chr…' and 'Install Con…' are truncated even though the column is about 140px wide and has room.
findings.fix: Allow labels to wrap to two lines, or widen the label box to the column width before ellipsizing.

findings.problem: The two thumbnails differ in size (about 216×118 vs 203×112) and their top edges are not aligned. They float with no border or selected state, so it is unclear which workspace is active.
findings.fix: Render both thumbnails at the same size on a shared baseline. Give the active workspace a 2px teal outline and the others a 1px neutral border.

findings.location: Overview workspace and the right edge
findings.problem: The overview shows a large empty workspace card, and the next workspace is clipped at the right screen edge as a tall dark sliver. The Activities button turns into a circle here but is a bare glyph in c01.
findings.fix: Keep the Activities button the same shape in every state, with a circular hover/active pill. Fade the adjacent workspace preview in, the way the GNOME reference does, rather than cutting it hard at the bezel.

findings.location: Quick settings tiles (Wired, Dark Style active)
findings.problem: The active state is teal text and icon on a slightly tinted teal fill, which is close in value to the inactive grey tiles and weak at a glance. Only Power Mode has a subtitle, so Wired doesn't show its connection state while Power Mode shows 'Balanced'.
findings.fix: Fill active tiles with solid teal and dark text (#0B1216) so on and off states differ in value, not just hue. Give every connection tile a subtitle line, for example 'Wired · Connected' and 'Caffeine · Off', so tile heights and information match.

findings.problem: The empty notification column takes about 60% of the popover for a single bell and 'No Notifications'. The 'Clear' button is still shown, greyed out, with nothing to clear. The calendar zero-pads days ('01', '05'), which looks like an identifier list rather than dates.
findings.fix: Shrink or hide the notification column when it is empty, and hide Clear when the list is empty. Use unpadded tabular numerals for day cells (1–31). Keep the monospace feel through tabular figures, not leading zeros.

findings.problem: The lock screen drops the wireframe room. Its background is a muddy blurred vignette with visible rectangular banding around the centre, and 'AM' is set at the same size and weight as the digits, which weakens the time. There is no 'press any key to unlock' hint, and the top bar shows indicators but no lock or user state.
findings.fix: Use a dimmed render of the wallpaper (the room at about 30% opacity) instead of a blur of a flat image, to remove the banding. Set the AM/PM marker at about 40% size or use 24h. Add a small 'Click or press a key to unlock' line in secondary text near the bottom.

findings.problem: The submit chevron is an oversized, thin grey glyph inside the field with no button shape, and it crowds the reveal-eye icon. The avatar is a generic placeholder at 128px, which dominates over the field, and 'Live session' sits tight against the field's 2px teal focus ring.
findings.fix: Make the submit a 32px circular teal button outside the field, or a proper inline icon button matched to the eye. Reduce the avatar to about 96px and add 12px between the name and the field.

findings.location: Top bar and dock at 100% scale
findings.problem: At the smaller scale the Vitals text drops to about 11px and the system icons shrink to about 12px, while the wallpaper stays the same size. The bar looks underweight and the Vitals numbers are hard to read on HiDPI.
findings.fix: Set a minimum panel text size (13px logical) and icon size (16px) that do not scale below the top bar height. Use tabular numerals for Vitals so the values don't jitter as they change.

findings.problem: The add control is a small uncontained “+” at the far edge; its relation to Wired is weak and it has a much smaller hit target than surrounding controls.
findings.fix: Use the same labeled or clearly bounded add affordance used across settings sections, with a minimum 32–40 px target.

findings.problem: The add action differs from c02: Wired uses a circular outlined icon button while VPN uses a bare plus. Equivalent actions do not share a visual treatment.
findings.fix: Standardize add actions across sections and screens; choose one target size, container treatment, and placement.

findings.problem: The theme cards are visibly clipped by the bottom of the modal, with no visible scrolling affordance or completion of the grid.
findings.fix: Make the picker area scroll independently and show a scrollbar/fade, or resize the dialog so complete card rows and actions remain visible.

findings.problem: The underlying editor’s header and content remain conspicuously visible around the modal, making the modal stack feel crowded and weakening focus.
findings.fix: Apply a clearer backdrop treatment and reduce distracting background contrast; ensure the modal has a more deliberate elevation relationship.

findings.problem: The light-mode surface turns the workspace into a nearly uniform pale gray field, and the wireframe-room brand mark is barely perceptible behind the window.
findings.fix: Provide a light-specific wallpaper/contrast treatment that preserves the room motif without competing with windows.

findings.problem: Card shadows, borders, and fills are substantially stronger than the surrounding light UI, so the chooser reads as a pasted dark-mode component rather than a cohesive light surface.
findings.fix: Reduce thumbnail elevation and harmonize borders, selected state, and surface tones with the light theme.

findings.location: System Monitor graphs and axis labels
findings.problem: Axis labels, time marks, and several metrics are very small and low-contrast at the shown scale, despite this screen being for reading operational data.
findings.fix: Increase minimum chart-label size and contrast, and simplify secondary labels so primary measurements remain scannable.

findings.problem: The screen presents a terminal conclusion—no disk available—but offers neither a recovery path nor an explanatory next step.
findings.fix: Add concise guidance and an available action such as rescan, open storage details, or documentation/help.

findings.location: Security keys, explanatory paragraph beneath heading
findings.problem: The explanatory copy is so low-contrast against the dark surface that it is difficult to read, including important security implications.
findings.fix: Raise secondary-text contrast to the established readable muted-text token and preserve it in all themes.

findings.problem: The content starts far from the sidebar and occupies a narrow upper-left region, leaving a large unused area that weakens hierarchy and scanning.
findings.fix: Use a deliberate readable content width with stronger alignment to the page title and cards, or introduce a contextual secondary panel rather than leaving the space inert.

findings.location: Preferences dialog over the Text Editor window
findings.problem: The modal sits on its parent with almost no separation. The parent's titlebar text ('Ope…', 'New Document') shows through above the dialog and is clipped. The dialog is offset, not centred on its parent, and its content is cut off mid-row at the bottom.
findings.fix: Dim the parent behind modals. Centre the dialog on its parent, with a stronger shadow and a lighter surface than the parent. Pad the scroll area, or fade its edge, so the clipped swatch row reads as scrollable.

findings.problem: Vitals shows '00 00 00' placeholders next to the icons. The values are meaningless, and the unit-less 00 reads like a fault.
findings.fix: Hide the bar's values until the first sample arrives, or show an em-dash. Give the readouts a fixed width so the clock doesn't shift.

findings.location: Light mode top bar and dock
findings.problem: In light mode the top bar stays solid dark navy and the dock is dark, over a pale grey-blue background. The wireframe room wallpaper is almost absent. The bar reads as heavy and not themed, while the windows are fully light.
findings.fix: Either follow the light scheme with a translucent light bar, or deliberately keep it dark and document that. Give the light wallpaper variant a visible room.

findings.problem: The wireframe room, which is the brand, shows only as a small teal corner fragment peeking above the window. Elsewhere the desktop is flat near-black, so the identity is lost at rest.
findings.fix: Show the wallpaper's room at a position the centred windows don't cover, or lower the windows' opacity so the wireframe reads.

findings.problem: The headerbar has the Files title and a kebab on the left, then arrows, path pill, a search-folder icon, a view toggle and a dropdown. The window controls are cramped at the far right. The 'Files' title is redundant next to the 'Home' path. Several icons have no visible pressed or hover affordance, and the view toggle icon is ambiguous.
findings.fix: Drop the redundant title, group the view controls, and give the toolbar buttons consistent hit areas with visible hover and active states.

findings.problem: The Desktop folder is a pale, differently rendered icon, so it looks like a different set. Projects has no emblem. The icon grid leaves a large empty area right and below.
findings.fix: Redraw Desktop in the same teal folder with a glyph. Give Projects a developer emblem such as a code or branch mark.

findings.problem: The content is sparse. The Wired row says only 'Connected', with no interface name, speed, IP or MAC, which is what developers want. The VPN 'Not set up' placeholder box is much taller and emptier than the other rows. Below Proxy about half the page is empty.
findings.fix: Show the interface name, speed and IP as secondary text in the Wired row. Make the empty VPN state the same height as a normal row, with an add action.

findings.problem: The sidebar is cut off at 'Mouse & Touchpad', with the row sliced by the window edge. There's no scroll indicator. The window is shorter than the content it needs.
findings.fix: Add a scroll fade or scrollbar, or make the default window taller.

findings.problem: The '+' buttons are bare glyphs with a small hit area and no visible affordance. In c03 the Wired one shows a circular hover ring, so the two states differ and the other '+' don't.
findings.fix: Use one flat button style with a 32px hit area and a clear hover ring on all of them.

findings.problem: The clock and metrics move left or right between screenshots (c02 versus c03) as the values change width, so the bar jitters. The CPU value shows '2.0' with no unit or label.
findings.fix: Use tabular numerals, a fixed minimum width for each readout, and a label or tooltip with the unit.

findings.problem: The terminal is a bare prompt in a window with no visible cursor and no colour. Its surface is almost the same as the other windows, so nothing marks it as the brand's flagship tool. The prompt 'bash-5.3$' is the generic default. The headerbar's tab/new icons are small and unlabeled.
findings.fix: Ship a branded prompt and palette, with a visible teal cursor and a distinct terminal background. Label the headerbar icons with tooltips.

findings.problem: The Resources graphs use saturated red, orange, yellow and green, plus bright blue and orange arrows. This works against the quiet teal system, and red and green carry status meaning without having any here. The tiny 10px axis labels are hard to read at 200% scale. The chart areas are blank grids because the data is only at the far right.
findings.fix: Re-theme the series palette to teal and neutral tints, with status colours only for alerts. Raise the axis labels to at least 11px and dim the grid.

findings.problem: The label-value pairs are loosely aligned, with the label and value in a ragged two-line block with different left edges. Numeric columns don't align between Receiving and Sending.
findings.fix: Use a two-column grid with right-aligned tabular numerals and secondary-coloured labels.

findings.problem: The window opens with an error ('This computer has no disk Construct can be installed on.') in plain body text with the same weight as a normal state. There's no next action, and a large empty area around the centred content. The logo is a muted grey-blue, unlike the teal brand colour.
findings.fix: Present the state as a clear empty or error state with a reason, a next step (for example 'Continue in live mode') and a primary button. Make the logo teal.

findings.problem: The help paragraph is small (about 11px), low-contrast grey on near-black, with a long line length. It carries the key explanation but is hard to read. The title 'Security keys' is repeated in the headerbar, the sidebar and the section.
findings.fix: Raise the contrast and size of the body text to the secondary-text token. Shorten it, and drop the repeated section heading.

findings.problem: The off switch is nearly invisible against its row, with a dark knob on a dark track. The 'No key added yet' card and the toggle card differ in radius, padding and background tint.
findings.fix: Give the off track a visible outline and lighter knob. Share one card style across both.

findings.problem: A clipboard icon appears between the clock and the Vitals readouts here, but not in the other screenshots, where it sits on the right. The bar's order shifts.
findings.fix: Pin the position of the indicators so they don't reorder.

findings.problem: The dock icons are in mixed styles: a flat VS Code logo, a gradient terminal and a calendar with a red header. Active-state indicators are tiny dots and the active tile is only slightly lighter. The calendar icon shows a fixed 'Friday 7' that doesn't match the bar's Oct 4.
findings.fix: Unify the icon treatment, enlarge the running-app indicator and make the calendar icon live.

findings.problem: The preview uses red 'Links' and orange bullets, both of which clash with the teal accent. The selected check badge is a bright cyan, unlike the teal in other screens.
findings.fix: Use one accent hue and its tints throughout.

findings.location: Top bar, Vitals cluster right of the clock
findings.problem: In light mode the Vitals readouts show '00 00 00' instead of the battery, load and network values. At a glance the system looks dead or the extension looks broken.
findings.fix: Fix the Vitals value rendering or font fallback under the light session so the bar shows real numbers, and add a light-mode capture to the gate that fails on placeholder digits.

findings.location: Text Editor Preferences dialog, top edge over the parent header bar
findings.problem: The dialog sits partly over the parent window's header bar. Parent labels ('Op…', 'New Document', icons) poke out above and around the dialog edge as clipped text. Same problem in c05.
findings.fix: Either show the parent's header in full above the dialog, or give the dialog its own scrim/dimming that hides the parent's header contents entirely. Never leave half-covered labels showing.

findings.location: Style-scheme grid, bottom of the Preferences dialog
findings.problem: The third row of scheme thumbnails is cut off hard at the dialog's bottom edge. There is no fade, scrollbar or padding, so it reads as a layout bug, not as scrollable content. Same in c05.
findings.fix: Size the dialog to fit whole rows, or add the bottom padding Orchis uses for scrolled content plus an overlay scrollbar or edge fade so the overflow reads as scrollable.

findings.problem: The preview has a 2px bright-teal outline that looks exactly like a keyboard focus ring. A static preview reads as a focused text field and takes the accent away from the actually selected scheme thumbnail.
findings.fix: Give the preview the neutral card border (same as the setting rows in c02). Keep the teal ring for focus and the selected thumbnail only.

findings.problem: The selection pill runs flush to the sidebar's left edge with square corners on the left and rounded corners on the right. Rows in the reference sidebars have inset, fully rounded pills. The same clipped pill shows up in c01 (Home), c03 and c09 (Security keys).
findings.fix: Inset the sidebar selection by the standard 6px on both sides and round all four corners. Make it one rule in the Orchis fork's navigation-sidebar row style.

findings.problem: The list is cut mid-row at the window's bottom edge. There is no fade or scroll hint, so the categories below are hard to find.
findings.fix: Add an edge fade or overlay-scrollbar hint at the bottom of scrolled sidebars, or open the window at a default height that ends on a group separator.

findings.problem: The Wired add button has a circular outlined background, while the identical VPN add button next to it is a bare glyph. c02 shows both bare. Hover or focus state is hard to tell from a style mismatch.
findings.fix: Make the hover/focus state of flat header buttons a filled tint (as on the sidebar) rather than an outline ring, so it can't be read as a different button type.

findings.location: 'Lock the screen when a key is unplugged' switch
findings.problem: The off switch is a dark knob on a dark track, almost invisible against the row's surface. Users can't easily see that a control is there or what state it's in. The on switch in c02 (cyan knob on teal track) is also low-contrast.
findings.fix: Give the off track a visible neutral fill (around 3:1 against the row) with a light knob. For on, use a teal track with a white knob, not cyan on teal.

findings.location: Security keys page, description paragraph under the heading
findings.problem: The most important explanation on the page is the smallest, dimmest text, about 11px in low-contrast grey across a long line. The page title is also repeated in both the header bar and the heading. Plain hyphens are used where dashes belong ('password - sudo').
findings.fix: Set the description in body size at secondary-text contrast (at least 4.5:1) and limit the line length to about 70ch. Drop the duplicate in-page heading or the header title. Use en/em dashes.

findings.problem: Here the clipboard indicator sits between the clock and the Vitals readouts. On every other screen it sits after them, so the status area reorders itself between sessions.
findings.fix: Pin the top-bar indicator order (clock, Vitals, then the extension icons) in the panel configuration so extensions can't insert themselves by load order.

findings.problem: 'Install Construct' is a dead end. The message says there's no disk, but there's no next step (try live, rescan, help). The large brand mark is flat grey, not the teal brand, so the one branded moment of the product feels disabled.
findings.fix: Add a primary action (Rescan disks) and a secondary link (Keep using the live system / Help), and draw the mark in the accent teal or the wireframe line style.

findings.location: System Monitor CPU legend and Memory pie
findings.problem: CPU cores are coded red/orange/yellow/green and memory is a red pie, so ordinary load reads as alarm states. The network and disk arrows also swap meaning: blue-down means receiving, but blue-up means reading.
findings.fix: Map per-core and memory series to a non-semantic palette built from the teal accent (teal, cyan, slate, violet), and use one direction and colour rule for in/out across network and disk.

findings.problem: Axis labels are about 7–8px and condensed, at the edge of legibility on HiDPI. The value readouts below are large and loosely laid out, and the section headers almost touch the previous section's legend.
findings.fix: Raise axis labels to the caption size (around 11px) using tabular numerals, and add one spacing step above each section header.

findings.problem: The wireframe-room wallpaper, the brand's main asset, is almost invisible: a single teal stroke shows behind the window. The desktop reads as flat near-black in c01, c02, c06, c07 and c09, so the system looks generic at rest.
findings.fix: Raise the wireframe stroke contrast or line weight in the dark wallpaper and frame the room so its main lines stay visible around a centered window, not only behind it.

findings.problem: The Desktop folder uses a different, lighter, flat-topped drawing than the other teal folders, so it looks like a leftover from another icon set.
findings.fix: Redraw the Desktop place icon in the Tela-fork folder template (same tab, fill and fold) with a desktop glyph.

findings.problem: The left half of the top bar holds only a small logo. There's no workspace or activities indicator and no focused-app name, so the bar's prime position says nothing about state. The right side packs about 12 dense glyphs.
findings.fix: Put a workspace indicator or the focused-app name next to the logo, and group the right-side status into Vitals | clock | system menu with consistent gaps.

findings.problem: VS Code's Microsoft blue, the blue/indigo terminal and the white paper calendar clash with the teal Tela-fork icons around them. The dock reads as three icon families.
findings.fix: Supply themed Tela-fork icons for the terminal and calendar in the teal palette, and add a matching teal-tinted override for the editor.

findings.location: Top bar and dock in light mode
findings.problem: In light mode the app chrome and wallpaper go light, but the top bar and dock stay near-black. The heavy frame fights the light content, and the light wallpaper loses the wireframe almost entirely.
findings.fix: Either commit to a dark shell on purpose and give it a lighter tint and a border for light sessions, or give the bar and dock a light variant. Ship a light wallpaper with enough line contrast for the room to show.

findings.problem: The flagship app opens to a bare 'bash-5.3$' prompt with the header title '~'. There's no user@host, no branded prompt, and nothing to show the verified image. The developer's main surface carries none of the product's identity.
findings.fix: Ship a default PS1 with user, host and cwd in the theme's accent colours, and use the cwd path as the header title instead of a bare '~'.

findings.problem: The light appearance reduces the room wallpaper to pale gray lines on a similarly pale field, losing both contrast and the product’s primary visual signature.
findings.fix: Provide a purpose-built light wallpaper treatment with substantially darker room lines and a light-background accent palette; verify contrast independently from the dark asset.

findings.problem: At this display scale the top bar, status indicators, and dock icons are markedly smaller and denser than in c01, making system state harder to scan on a HiDPI developer desktop.
findings.fix: Set scale-aware minimum hit targets and type/icon sizing for shell chrome, rather than allowing the chrome to shrink proportionally with the display.

findings.problem: A second workspace/window preview is clipped into a narrow rounded slab at the right edge, reading as an accidental fragment rather than an intentional carousel or workspace.
findings.fix: Either fit the adjacent preview with a clear gutter and visible label, or omit it until it can be presented as a complete, navigable card.

findings.problem: The search field floats separately above a single oversized preview with no workspace/app context, while a large amount of empty black space remains.
findings.fix: Use an overview layout with explicit workspace grouping and consistently sized previews; align search, previews, and dock to one centered content grid.

findings.problem: Two nearly identical unlabeled room thumbnails consume prominent space above the app grid, but do not communicate their role or offer clear selection state.
findings.fix: Label these as workspace/window previews and add clear active/hover treatment, or remove them from the app-grid view to preserve a direct launcher hierarchy.

findings.problem: Several application names are truncated inconsistently (for example, “Google Chr...” and “Install Con...”), despite ample unused horizontal space in the overall layout.
findings.fix: Use a responsive grid column width or a tooltip/full-name secondary treatment so common developer tools remain identifiable.

findings.problem: Notification cards overlap each other and collide with the panel boundary; titles and body copy are visibly layered and unreadable.
findings.fix: Enforce vertical card stacking with fixed gaps, clipping, and overflow behavior before showing additional notifications.

findings.problem: The empty notification region dominates the left half of a very wide flyout while the calendar and actions are compressed into the right side.
findings.fix: Use a narrower calendar-only panel when there are no notifications, or rebalance the split so the empty state does not create a dead zone.

findings.problem: Only a small cluster of status/action icons remains visible, detached from a panel and without labels, which makes their purpose and state unclear on the lock screen.
findings.fix: Use a coherent lock-screen status bar or hide nonessential controls; retain only clearly discoverable power/accessibility actions.

findings.problem: The password field’s oversized teal outline and large arrow dominate the otherwise quiet screen, while the low-contrast username and avatar provide weak account context.
findings.fix: Reserve teal for focus/active state, reduce the submit affordance, and strengthen account-name/avatar contrast and hierarchy.

findings.location: Notification list in the calendar popover
findings.problem: Notification cards render on top of each other. 'Disk almost full' and 'Wired connection established' overlap with garbled text, and two System headers and two close buttons collide. The banner at top-left is also clipped behind the popover.
findings.fix: Fix the message-list layout so each card gets its own row, with consistent spacing and no negative margins or duplicated stacked groups. Keep the toast banner from sliding under the popover.

findings.problem: Vitals show '00 00 00' with no units, so the readings are meaningless. Elsewhere the bar shows 45%, 0.8 and 33 KB/s, so it looks like a failure state.
findings.fix: Show a real placeholder such as '–' or hold the last value. Make sure the metrics have units and never render a zero-padded '00'.

findings.problem: There are about 12 undifferentiated items. The Vitals icons and values are tightly packed and the gaps are irregular. The date and time have nearly the same weight as the metrics, and the layout/clipboard icons are unlabeled. Nothing reads first.
findings.fix: Group the items as clock, then metrics, then system. Add a consistent gap between groups. Make the clock the strongest element, mute the metrics, and drop rarely used icons.

findings.problem: The clock is off-centre and sits among the metrics. Neither the date nor the time is anchored, and the clock changes position between screens (c01 vs c02/c03) as the Vitals widths change.
findings.fix: Centre the clock, as GNOME and macOS do, and give the Vitals fixed-width tabular fields so the layout doesn't shift.

findings.location: Dock calendar icon and app icons
findings.problem: The calendar icon is a bright white tile with red text and reads 'FRIDAY 7', while the top bar says Oct 4/5. The icons also mix styles: teal Tela-fork icons next to VS Code blue, a purple-blue terminal and a white calendar. There are no running-app indicators.
findings.fix: Make the calendar icon follow the real date or use a neutral icon. Recolour third-party icons into the palette, or give them a consistent backplate. Add running dots under the dock icons.

findings.problem: The two workspace thumbnails at the top are small dark boxes with different sizes and no active-state ring. The icon grid is left-aligned with a ragged last row, and labels are truncated ('Google Chr...', 'Install Con...'). Two Construct icons sit in the same grid, and the folders show a heavy dark tile.
findings.fix: Make the workspace thumbnails equal size with a clear active state, or hide them in the grid. Allow two-line labels or widen the cells. Remove the duplicate icon. Centre the grid.

findings.problem: The overview shows a single huge workspace card with no windows and a clipped neighbour at the right edge. The search field is low-contrast, the card is nearly the same colour as the background, and the top bar clock sits next to the Activities button with no pill. The black surround differs from the desktop's navy.
findings.fix: Use the same background colour as the desktop. Raise the search field's contrast and give the active workspace a subtle border. Hide the clipped neighbour when there is only one workspace.

findings.problem: The tile states are unclear. Wired and Dark Style are teal-tinted with cyan text, but the contrast between on and off is small. Wired is on but Power Mode is not, and the two use different layouts (arrow split vs plain). The panel is missing brightness, battery and Bluetooth, and the top-row icons are unlabeled and small. The tile text is bold and tight.
findings.fix: Use a solid teal fill with dark text for 'on', and a neutral fill for 'off'. Make the tiles consistent in height and arrow treatment. Add the missing sliders and state indicators.

findings.problem: The empty notifications half takes about 55% of the popover with a lone bell and a dim 'Clear' button. The calendar uses zero-padded dates (01, 02) and very small letters, and the weekday header is faint. The event buttons are low-contrast grey on grey and the today highlight is the only accent.
findings.fix: Collapse or narrow the notifications column when it is empty. Drop the zero-padding on the dates and raise the contrast of the weekday headers and secondary text.

findings.problem: The lock screen is almost featureless: a big clock and a faint vignette, with none of the wireframe-room brand. The top right keeps the network, volume and power icons with no battery indicator. The date is small and the clock is huge, so the scale jump is abrupt. There is no hint such as 'swipe up' or 'press a key'.
findings.fix: Show the room wallpaper at low contrast, add a hint line, and include the battery and notification status. Soften the clock weight and size the date up a step.

findings.problem: The input holds a single dot and a cursor, with no placeholder or label. The submit arrow is grey and oversized next to the small eye icon, and the avatar is a generic person glyph. 'Live session' as a name is a placeholder. The field fill is lighter than the cyan focus ring would suggest, so it looks heavy.
findings.fix: Add a 'Password' placeholder, make the arrow match the eye in size and make it teal when enabled. Use a branded avatar and a real username. Add an error/caps-lock area under the field.

findings.problem: The light-mode wallpaper is a pale grey-blue with a washed-out grey wireframe, so the teal brand colour disappears. The top bar and dock stay dark navy, which gives a heavy contrast with the pale desktop. The icons were designed for dark and the bar is not themed.
findings.fix: Use a teal accent for the wireframe's main edges in light mode. Theme the bar and dock lighter, or deliberately keep them dark with a softer edge.

findings.problem: At the smaller scale the bar is 30px tall with tiny 10px text, and the metrics' glyphs touch their values. The dock is smaller and its icon sizes differ from c01, which shows the sizes aren't scaled with the bar.
findings.fix: Set the bar and dock sizes from a single scale token. Keep the minimum text size at 12 and the icon-to-value gap constant.

findings.problem: The bar is a rounded pill floating at the edge with only a faint border, but in c04 and c05 the bar disappears into black. The Activities button has an unusual workspace icon and no label, so it is not discoverable.
findings.fix: Use the same bar treatment in every view and give the Activities button a hover/active state and a tooltip.

findings.location: Notification list, top of left column in the calendar menu
findings.problem: Two notifications ('Connected / Wired connection established' and 'Disk almost full / Only 2.1 GB…') are drawn on top of each other. Headers, titles and bodies overlap and can't be read. The close and expand buttons sit on top of each other too, and a ghost card edge shows below.
findings.fix: Fix the message-list stacking in the theme. Give grouped notifications their own allocation (no negative margins or fixed heights on .message), so each card gets its full height and a consistent gap (8px) between cards. Then retest with 2 or more notifications from the same app.

findings.problem: The incoming banner is drawn underneath the open calendar menu and clipped at its left edge. Its body text is cut off at 'copied t'.
findings.fix: Suppress or queue banners while the date menu is open (GNOME's default), or raise the banner above the menu layer. Don't let two surfaces overlap at the same time.

findings.location: Top bar, Vitals cluster (memory / load / network)
findings.problem: Vitals shows '00 00 00' placeholders instead of values. When the date menu is open, the at-a-glance system state disappears, so the readout looks broken. Same in c08.
findings.fix: Keep the last sampled values while menus are open. Show an em dash '—' only when no reading exists yet, never zero-padded placeholders.

findings.problem: The calendar app icon shows a static 'FRIDAY 7', but the system date is Monday 4/5 October. A date that disagrees with the clock is a false state signal on every screen with the dock (c01–c08).
findings.fix: Use a non-dated calendar glyph from the Tela fork, or a dynamic calendar icon that renders today's weekday and date.

findings.location: Top bar, right cluster: clipboard and layout icons
findings.problem: The clipboard and tiling-layout indicators swap order between screens (c01 and c06: clipboard then layout; c02 and c03: layout then clipboard). Icons that move around break muscle memory.
findings.fix: Pin indicator order in the panel config (Dash to Panel / extension position indices) so the order is the same in every session and mode.

findings.location: Top bar, between the clock and Vitals
findings.problem: Date, time, memory %, load and network rate run together as one line of equal-weight text with uneven gaps. The clock doesn't read first. The monitor glyph means 'load' in Vitals and 'wired network' in the status area at the same time.
findings.fix: Group the cluster as [Vitals] | [date time] | [system status] with a 16px gap or a hairline between groups. Use tabular numerals and fixed widths for the Vitals values. Give load a distinct glyph (e.g. a gauge) so the monitor icon only means display or wired network.

findings.location: Top bar and dock in light style
findings.problem: In light style the panel and dock stay near-black navy slabs on a pale grey desktop. That's the heaviest contrast on screen at rest, which fights the 'calm' brief. The wallpaper also drops the teal for neutral grey, so light mode loses the brand accent.
findings.fix: Ship a light panel and dock surface (e.g. #F4F6F8 at 85% with a 1px border in the dark-ink colour at 10%). Draw the light wallpaper's main room edges in a darker teal (accent darkened to meet 3:1 on the background) instead of grey.

findings.location: Workspace thumbnails above the app grid
findings.problem: The two workspace thumbnails are different sizes and their tops don't line up (left about 216×118, right about 203×111). The gap from thumbnails to the first icon row is about 80px, larger than the gap between rows.
findings.fix: Render the thumbnails at the same scale with aligned tops. Reduce the gap above the grid to match the row spacing (about 40–48px).

findings.location: App grid labels and icon set
findings.problem: Labels are cut off ('Google Chr…', 'Install Con…'). Icons mix the Tela flat style (Construct, Calculator, Settings) with Adwaita and vendor styles (Clocks, Camera, Characters, Vim, 1Password), so the grid doesn't read as one family. The folder tiles are the only items with filled backgrounds.
findings.fix: Allow 2-line labels in the app grid. Add Tela-fork overrides for Clocks, Camera, Characters, Text Editor and Vim. Give the folder tiles the same hover-only background as app tiles, or a 1px outline instead of a solid fill.

findings.problem: The overview backdrop is pure #000, while every other surface uses the navy ink (#0B1117-ish). The workspace card looks like a lighter rectangle on a void, and the next workspace peeks in at the right edge as a flat slab.
findings.fix: Tint the overview background with the system's darkest navy, and give workspace cards the standard card radius and shadow, so the overview feels like the same room as the desktop.

findings.location: Quick settings: active toggles 'Wired' and 'Dark Style'
findings.problem: Active state is shown as teal text and icon on a dark-teal tint. The active and inactive pills are close in luminance, and teal on dark teal is low contrast. Toggles with chevrons (Wired, Caffeine) split the pill with a hairline. Caffeine's chevron is inconsistent, since it has no submenu meaning.
findings.fix: Fill active toggles with the solid accent and dark ink text (as in the macOS reference, where on-state is unmistakable). Keep inactive pills neutral. Remove the menu arrow from toggles that have no real submenu.

findings.problem: Days are zero-padded ('01', '05', '07'), which reads like a data table rather than a calendar. Days from the previous and next month have nearly the same weight as the current month. The empty notifications column takes about 60% of the menu width for one bell icon.
findings.fix: Drop the zero-padding. Dim days outside the current month to the secondary text colour. Narrow the notification column when it's empty, or move the empty-state copy up so the menu feels balanced.

findings.problem: The lock screen shows the clock on an almost-black, blurred blob. The wireframe room (the brand) disappears entirely. There's no hint how to unlock and no notification count, so the screen gives no state at a glance.
findings.fix: Show the room wallpaper dimmed (e.g. 40% brightness, light blur) behind the clock. Add a small 'Click or press a key to unlock' line and a notification summary under the date.

findings.location: Unlock prompt: password field and submit chevron
findings.problem: The 2px saturated cyan focus ring is the loudest element on the screen. The large grey chevron sits half outside the field's inner padding and doesn't match the eye icon's size. There's no visible way to go back or switch users, and the avatar is the generic placeholder for 'Live session'.
findings.fix: Use a 2px ring in the accent at reduced opacity, or a 1px outline with a soft glow. Put the submit control inside the field as a 32px circular button matching the eye icon's weight. Add a 'Cancel' or back affordance below the field. Use the Construct mark as the default avatar for the live user.

findings.location: Top bar and dock at the lower scale
findings.problem: At the smaller display scale, the top-bar text (about 11px) and Vitals glyphs become very small. The dock shrinks while the top bar keeps the same rounded inset, so the proportions between bar, dock and wallpaper change.
findings.fix: Set a minimum top-bar font size of about 13px at 100%, and scale panel height, dock icon size and inset margins together so the composition holds across scales.

findings.problem: The standalone plus glyph has little visible hit area or button treatment, making its action and target ambiguous.
findings.fix: Use the same clearly bounded circular add control shown in c03, with a consistent accessible hit target.

findings.problem: The window cuts off the final row of theme choices without a visible scroll affordance, so available options appear incomplete.
findings.fix: Constrain the grid to a scrollable area with a visible scrollbar, or resize the dialog to show complete cards and their labels.

findings.location: Preferences modal over the editor window
findings.problem: A large modal sits over another window whose title bar and controls remain visibly exposed, creating unclear window ownership and competing chrome.
findings.fix: Make the preferences surface clearly application-modal with a subdued parent, or present it as a normal independent window with its own full frame.

findings.problem: The light theme shifts from the restrained dark system to a bright blue-grey canvas with strong shadows and low-contrast inactive surfaces, weakening the calm technical character.
findings.fix: Use a warmer, quieter light neutral palette, reduce elevation shadows, and increase separation between dialog, cards, and disabled/background content.

findings.location: Resources monitor, graph axes and live metric labels
findings.problem: Axis labels, time markers, and several secondary metric values are too small and faint for rapid scanning on a HiDPI desktop.
findings.fix: Increase the minimum size and contrast of graph labels, reduce redundant tick text, and give live values stronger typographic priority.

findings.problem: The screen reports that no installable disk exists but provides neither recovery guidance nor an action to refresh, inspect storage, or exit.
findings.fix: Add a concise explanation of likely causes plus actionable controls such as Refresh disks, Storage details, and Quit.

findings.location: Security keys, explanatory paragraph beneath heading
findings.problem: The explanatory copy is markedly lower contrast than the rest of the interface, despite containing important security behavior.
findings.fix: Raise body-text contrast to the standard secondary-text token and preserve that token across settings pages.

findings.problem: The folder tiles are widely spaced while labels sit relatively close to the icons, producing a sparse, uneven rhythm in the final row.
findings.fix: Use a consistent grid cell height and row/column gap so partially filled rows retain the same visual cadence.

findings.location: Preferences dialog over the Text Editor window
findings.problem: The modal sits offset over its parent. The parent's titlebar text is clipped and bleeds through ('Ope…', 'N…D…'). The wireframe wallpaper fragment pokes out above the window. The dialog's own content is cut off at the bottom with half-visible swatches.
findings.fix: Dim the parent and hide its header controls while a modal is open, or center the modal fully on top of it. Make the dialog scroll with a visible scrollbar or fade, and don't show a half-cut row.

findings.problem: The top bar and dock stay dark navy against a pale grey-blue wallpaper. The bar has a hard edge with no light variant, and the Vitals readouts show '00 00 00' placeholders. The wallpaper is a flat fill with no wireframe room.
findings.fix: Define a deliberate light-mode shell. Either theme the bar and dock for light, or state that they stay dark and tune their contrast and border. Show real Vitals values and a light-mode room wallpaper.

findings.location: Light and dark swatches in the Preferences dialog
findings.problem: The highlighted markdown preview box uses a bright cyan outline in dark mode and a different teal in light mode. The first swatch's selection ring is white in both modes, so it doesn't use the accent.
findings.fix: Use one accent token for focus and selection rings. Keep the preview box border neutral.

findings.problem: The Desktop folder icon is a pale, flat, different style from the other teal folders. Projects has no glyph. The grid fills only the top-left of a large empty window, and the sidebar lists only 5 items.
findings.fix: Give Desktop and Projects glyphs in the same folder style, with matching fill and contrast. Size the default window to its content, or add useful sidebar entries such as pinned folders.

findings.problem: The sidebar title area ('Files' with a menu) and the path bar share one crowded row. The kebab menu appears twice. The view and sort icons are tiny, and the window controls are small and low-contrast compared with the toolbar.
findings.fix: Remove the duplicate kebab and group the view controls. Make the window-control glyphs larger and lift their contrast.

findings.problem: The Wired row is labelled only 'Connected' with no interface name, speed or address. The '+' buttons are bare glyphs, but in c03 the Wired '+' gets a hover ring. The sidebar is cut off at 'Mouse & Touchpad' with no scroll hint.
findings.fix: Show the interface name and IP in the Wired row. Give '+' a consistent hover and focus state, and add a fade or scrollbar at the clipped sidebar edge.

findings.problem: Most of the right pane is empty. The section headers (Wired, VPN, Proxy) are bold white, the same weight as the page title, so levels aren't clearly separated. The 'Not set up' VPN block is a large empty box.
findings.fix: Use a smaller, dimmer section-header style. Collapse the empty VPN state into a compact row with an 'Add VPN' action.

findings.problem: The terminal is almost empty. The prompt 'bash-5.3$' is plain, and the text is small and thin for a developer's main surface. The header icons (new tab, grid, kebab) are tiny, and the title '~' is minimal.
findings.fix: Ship a branded prompt and a larger default font with a defined terminal palette using the teal accent. Show a tab bar only when needed, and size the header icons consistently.

findings.problem: The graphs use saturated rainbow colours: red, orange, yellow, green and blue arrows. This breaks the calm teal system, and red and green carry no clear status meaning. The axis labels are tiny and low-contrast. The legend swatches are heavy flat blocks, and the sections have little separation.
findings.fix: Use a restrained series palette built around the teal accent, with red reserved for alerts. Raise the axis label size and contrast. Use slimmer legend dots and add spacing between sections.

findings.problem: The screen shows a bare error message ('no disk…') with no next step. The grey logo is oversized, the dead space below is large, and there is no action button or explanation. Text is centred in a large window.
findings.fix: Add a clear next action (Try Construct, Learn more, Close) and explain the state. Use the teal brand mark and reduce the window size.

findings.problem: The description paragraph is dim grey on dark at small size, and its contrast is too low for important security text. It runs about 100 characters per line. The 'No key added yet' card and the 'Add a key' action both look like list rows. The off toggle is nearly invisible against its card. The right pane has large unused space.
findings.fix: Raise the body-text contrast and cap the measure near 70 characters. Make 'Add a key' a clear primary button. Give the off toggle a visible track outline.

findings.problem: The clipboard icon moves to a different position in the bar than in other screens, so the bar layout shifts. The clock and Vitals text are small, and the icon cluster on the right has uneven spacing.
findings.fix: Fix the order and width of bar items. Use tabular figures for the Vitals values so the bar doesn't jitter.

findings.problem: The app icons come from different styles: teal Tela, a blue VS Code logo, a blue terminal, and a calendar that shows a fixed 'FRIDAY 7' on a Saturday-or-Sunday screen. The running-app indicator is a tiny dot. The active app tile is only faintly highlighted.
findings.fix: Recolour third-party icons into the Tela fork. Make the running dot larger, and give the focused app a clearer highlight.

findings.location: Top bar, Vitals readouts right of the clock
findings.problem: In light mode Vitals shows placeholder values '00  00  00' instead of CPU, load and network figures, and the top bar stays dark navy while everything else switches to light. The bar's live system readout fails in exactly the mode where the bar was not restyled.
findings.fix: Make Vitals show real values whenever the theme changes, and give the top bar a light-mode palette, or explicitly declare it always-dark and test it that way. Add a light-mode screenshot test that fails on '00' placeholders.

findings.location: Text editor Preferences dialog over its parent window (top edge, y≈185–230)
findings.problem: The dialog sits partly over the parent's header bar, so the parent's title ('New Document'), its 'Open' button and its header icons are cut through and half-visible above the dialog. It looks like a rendering glitch, not a modal. c05 has the same problem, and there the parent is dimmed to flat grey, which makes the overlap even more obvious.
findings.fix: Show the preferences as a full-size modal centered over the parent with a consistent dim scrim that hides the parent's header controls, or open it as its own window. The dialog should never overlap the parent's title by a few pixels.

findings.location: Preferences, style-scheme grid at the bottom
findings.problem: The third row of scheme thumbnails is cut off at the dialog's bottom edge, with no fade or scrollbar. The Markdown preview takes the top half, so there is no visible sign that more schemes exist.
findings.fix: Make the dialog taller so at least three full rows fit, or show an overlay scrollbar or bottom fade on the scroll area. Shrinking the preview to about 4 lines also frees a row.

findings.location: Preferences, Markdown preview border and selected scheme card
findings.problem: Selection is shown two ways next to each other: the preview has a 2px saturated cyan border, while the selected scheme card has a white border plus a cyan check. The preview isn't even selectable, yet it carries the strongest accent on the screen, which breaks the 'calm at rest' rule.
findings.fix: Give the preview a neutral 1px border. Show selection only on the chosen scheme card, using the accent for both its border and its check, as GTK's accent role intends.

findings.problem: The calendar icon is a static image showing 'FRIDAY 7', while the top bar says Oct 4, Oct 5 or Oct 13 depending on the screen. In a system about verified state, an icon that shows a wrong date is noticeable. Its white and red tile also clashes with the teal dock set.
findings.fix: Show the current date on the calendar icon (as GNOME Calendar's dynamic icon can), or use a dateless calendar glyph in the Tela-fork teal palette.

findings.location: Dock, terminal icon, and the VS Code icon next to it
findings.problem: The terminal icon is periwinkle blue-purple with a white chip, and VS Code is its brand blue. For a developer desktop, the most-used app breaks the teal icon family, so the dock reads as three different palettes.
findings.fix: Redraw the terminal icon in the Tela-fork teal family: a dark slate tile with a teal prompt glyph, matching the Construct mark's line weight. Leave third-party brand icons alone, but make the system's own icons a unified set.

findings.location: Top bar, clipboard icon between the clock and Vitals
findings.problem: On this screen the clipboard indicator sits left of the Vitals group; on every other screen it sits right of the network rate. The Vitals values also change width (0 B/s vs 228 B/s), so the clock moves horizontally between screens (x≈904 to 947). The top bar's layout isn't stable.
findings.fix: Pin the extension order (clock, Vitals, clipboard, quick settings), and give each Vitals readout fixed-width tabular numerals with a minimum width so the clock never moves.

findings.location: Top bar Vitals icons (chip, monitor, cloud)
findings.problem: Bare numbers like '2.1' next to a monitor icon and '42%' next to a chip icon don't say what they measure (load average? memory?). A monitor glyph reads as 'display', not 'load'. Developers can't read the system state at a glance.
findings.fix: Use clear glyphs (CPU chip for CPU %, a gauge or 'load' glyph for load average, memory module for RAM) and show units, or a tooltip listing all three metrics. Keep numbers in tabular figures.

findings.location: Security keys, description paragraph under the section title
findings.problem: The most important explanation on the page (what a key unlocks, and that you should add a backup) is set at about 11px in low-contrast grey and wraps across a long line. It's the least legible text on screen while also being the key decision-making copy. Spaced hyphens ' - ' stand in for dashes.
findings.fix: Set the description at body size (about 14px) in the dim-label colour at ≥4.5:1 contrast, cap the measure at about 70ch, and use proper em dashes. Consider moving 'Add a second key…' into its own info row.

findings.location: 'Lock the screen when a key is unplugged' switch
findings.problem: The off switch is a dark knob on a nearly identical dark track inside a slightly lighter card, so it barely shows as a control. The ON switch in c02 is vivid teal, so off and on aren't a balanced pair.
findings.fix: Give the off track a visible neutral fill (e.g. 15–20% foreground) and a light knob, matching libadwaita's off switch, so the control is visible before it is turned on.

findings.location: Left sidebar icons vs. Settings sidebar (c02)
findings.problem: The Construct app's sidebar uses filled glyphs (shield, gear, battery), while GNOME Settings uses outlined symbolic icons. The Tailscale glyph reads as a lock or bell. The card fills also differ: the key list card is darker than the 'Lock the screen' row.
findings.fix: Draw Construct's sidebar icons as outlined symbolic icons on the same 16px grid as Settings, give Tailscale a network-mesh glyph, and use one boxed-list fill for all row groups on the page.

findings.location: Files sidebar selected row 'Home' vs. Settings selected row (c02)
findings.problem: In Files the selected pill is inset, with the icon nearly touching its left edge. In Settings and the Construct app the pill runs to the window edge with square left corners. The same sidebar component has two shapes.
findings.fix: Use one selected-row geometry for all sidebars: inset 6px from both edges, fully rounded, with 12px inner padding before the icon.

findings.problem: Desktop is a lighter, flatter teal tile with a window glyph, unlike the other eight folders' darker tabbed teal folder shape. It looks like a different icon set.
findings.fix: Redraw Desktop with the same folder silhouette and teal value as the others, with a small desktop/monitor emblem.

findings.location: System Monitor, CPU legend and memory pie
findings.problem: CPU1 is red, CPU2 orange, CPU3 yellow, CPU4 green, and the memory pie is red at 52%. These are traffic-light status colours used as identities, so a normal load looks like an alarm. Network 'Receiving' (down arrow) and disk 'Reading' (up arrow) share blue but point opposite ways.
findings.fix: Use a non-semantic categorical palette (teal, blue, violet and slate tints) for per-core series. Save red and orange for thresholds. Give read and receive the same direction and colour, and write and send the other.

findings.problem: The axis and tick labels are about 6px at this scale, below legible size on HiDPI, while the section headers are 14px bold. The data is the point of the window, but its scale can't be read.
findings.fix: Set tick labels to at least the caption size (≈11px logical) in dim-label colour, and drop the x-axis labels to three ticks (1 min, 30 s, now).

findings.problem: It's an error state presented as a hero: there's a large logo and 'This computer has no disk Construct can be installed on.', but no action, no details, no way forward. The body text is full white rather than secondary, so there's no hierarchy under the title.
findings.fix: Add a primary action ('Show disks' or 'Try again') and a secondary 'Keep using the live session'. Mark the state as an error with a short reason (e.g. 'Needs 64 GB; largest disk is 32 GB'). Set the body in the dim-label style.

findings.problem: For a developer audience, the wired row says only 'Connected', with no interface name, IP or speed. The page is about 60% empty while the useful facts are one click away behind the gear.
findings.fix: Show a subtitle on the row (e.g. 'enp3s0 · 192.168.1.24 · 1 Gb/s') in monospace or tabular figures, using the space the empty state leaves free.

findings.problem: The brand wallpaper, the wireframe room, is almost never visible: the desktop reads as flat near-black, and the only trace is a teal line fragment behind the window in c01 and c04. That fragment looks like a stray rendering artifact, not a brand element. Windows have almost no shadow, so they float on a void.
findings.fix: Lay out the wallpaper so the room's main lines frame the default window area rather than hiding behind it (e.g. the vanishing point off-centre, lines visible at the edges). Give windows a soft ambient shadow in dark mode so they separate from the background.

pairs.reason: The visible difference is only live system-state text, not the UI design.
Its teal wireframe preserves the product’s defining accent and reads more intentionally on the light surface.
The layouts and component treatment are materially the same; only frozen status data differs.
The overview composition and component styling are materially identical.
It exposes the complete app set, including Trayscale, so the grid is more useful for launching.
The quick-settings layout, hierarchy, and states are materially the same.
The brighter cyan selected date has clearer state feedback against the dense calendar.
Its notification cards maintain readable, non-overlapping text.
The clock sits in a calmer upper-third lock-screen position, leaving room for the wallpaper’s focal glow.
The unlock form and visual treatment are materially identical.

findings.problem: The empty notification half remains very large while the calendar and utility rows are compressed into the other half, creating an unbalanced panel with wasted space.
findings.fix: Use adaptive columns: collapse or substantially narrow the empty notification area, or give calendar and notifications separate popovers.

findings.problem: A partially visible neighboring workspace/card is clipped at the edge without enough context to communicate that horizontal navigation is available.
findings.fix: Show an intentional workspace carousel edge treatment with a visible next card and navigation affordance, or fit the available workspaces cleanly.

findings.problem: App names such as “Google Chr...” and “Install Con...” truncate without a visible way to disambiguate them.
findings.fix: Allocate a slightly wider grid or provide full-name hover/focus labels and preserve distinctive leading words.

findings.problem: Notification titles and body copy overlap, making multiple alerts unreadable.
findings.fix: Give each notification an independent vertical layout with measured text wrapping and stack spacing; constrain or collapse older cards.

findings.problem: The large right-arrow submit icon is visually much heavier than the eye toggle and competes with the password-entry affordance.
findings.fix: Reduce the arrow’s weight or place it in a discrete trailing button while retaining a clear keyboard-submit cue.

pairs.reason: Vitals have a proper gap between icon and value (38%, 0.9, 13 B/s), so readings scan cleanly; in a the icons are jammed against the numbers.
The teal wireframe in light mode keeps the brand accent and identity, and the top-bar vitals have breathing room. b's grey room loses the brand and the icons crowd the values.
At the smaller scale the vitals in a keep a little more icon-to-value separation. Otherwise the two are nearly identical.
Identical overview layouts. The only difference is the frozen vitals, which is not a product defect.
Same app grid. The only difference is one extra app (Trayscale) and the vitals, so there is no design difference.
The on-state tile in a is a quiet dark-teal tint with cyan label, which suits a calm system. b's saturated teal fill makes the cyan label and icon low-contrast and louder.
Today is marked by a muted teal-tint disc with cyan numeral, so the calendar stays calm. a's solid bright cyan disc is the loudest object on screen.
b has two notifications rendered on top of each other, with overlapping text and icons, which is a broken state. a shows a clean single notification.
Only the clock's vertical position differs. a sits high like the macOS reference and b nearer the optical centre. Neither adds identity, since both are a plain dark void.
Pixel-identical login screens.

findings.location: Notification list in the calendar popover, top-left card
findings.problem: The 'Connected' and 'Disk almost full' notifications are stacked at the same position. Titles, bodies and the dismiss and expand buttons overprint each other and are unreadable. The banner also clips 'Backup finished … copied t' under the popover.
findings.fix: Fix the notification group stacking so each card gets its own row, or collapse to one card with a count. Make the toast banner and the popover mutually exclusive, or offset the banner so it is never clipped.

findings.problem: The lock screen is a near-black void with a clock. The wireframe room is absent, so the most-seen moment of the product carries no brand identity. The top-right icon cluster floats with no bar.
findings.fix: Put the room in the lock background, dim and large, at the same position as the desktop. Keep the clock as the one bright element. Group or label the top-right status icons.

findings.problem: The password field shows one dot and a caret with no label or placeholder. 'Live session' is the only identifier. The chevron submit button is oversized and the eye icon is tiny and crowded beside it. The heavy cyan ring is the loudest element on a calm screen.
findings.fix: Add a 'Password' placeholder and shrink the submit chevron to the field's icon scale. Use a thinner, lower-chroma focus ring. Replace the generic avatar glyph with a brand mark or a teal-tinted tile.

findings.location: Top bar Vitals cluster (memory, CPU, network)
findings.problem: Icon-to-value gaps differ between readings and between captures ('45%' touching its icon, '38%' spaced). The values change width, so the cluster jitters and the clock shifts left or right.
findings.fix: Give each Vitals item a fixed icon gap and a tabular-figure fixed-width value box. Reserve space for the widest value. Add a small separator between the clock and Vitals.

findings.location: Light mode top bar and dock
findings.problem: In light mode the top bar and dock stay dark navy slabs on a pale background. The dock has no running-app indicators. The right-side icon order also changes between light and dark (layout and clipboard swap), so the same control moves.
findings.fix: Use a light translucent bar and dock in light mode, or commit to dark chrome as a deliberate choice. Keep the icon order identical in both modes.

findings.problem: The grey room on a pale blue-grey ground is low contrast and drops the teal accent. It reads as a different brand.
findings.fix: Use the teal-line room for light mode too, with lines darkened enough for contrast.

findings.location: Notification and calendar popover, left column and footer
findings.problem: The left half of the popover is a large empty panel with a low-contrast 'Clear' control. The calendar shows 'Today / No Events', 'Add World Clocks…' and 'Select Weather Location…' as dim grey on slightly lighter grey, which is hard to read. The weekday and month header is unevenly weighted.
findings.fix: Shrink the notification column when it is empty. Raise the label contrast to at least 4.5:1. Hide or move the setup prompts to Settings. Align 'Clear' with the other controls.

findings.problem: On-state tiles have only a faint tint and a thin cyan label, so on/off is hard to tell from the neutral tiles at a glance. In b, cyan text on a saturated teal fill is low contrast. Power Mode has no state colour at all, and Caffeine and Wired carry arrows while the others do not.
findings.fix: Make one on-state treatment: solid teal fill with dark text, or tint plus an indicator. Apply it to every toggle, and state it in the label ('On'/'Off' subtitle).

findings.location: App grid labels and icon set
findings.problem: Labels truncate ('Google Chr…', 'Install Con…'). Third-party icons (Chrome, 1Password, Maps, Music) are full-colour and clash with the teal Tela-fork family. The grid is left-heavy and ends in a ragged last row. The two workspace thumbnails at the top are small, low-contrast, and unequal in size.
findings.fix: Widen the label area or allow two lines. Recolour or mask the fallback icons to the theme. Centre the last row. Make the workspace thumbnails equal and larger with a clear active state.

findings.problem: The empty workspace shows a big dark card with a smaller wireframe and a cropped neighbour. There are no window previews to judge the window-switching design, and the card is only slightly lighter than the black background.
findings.fix: Increase the card-to-background contrast, add a thin teal outline for the active workspace, and verify window thumbnails and titles on a populated overview.

findings.problem: The dock is small for a 200% screen. The calendar icon shows a hard-coded 'FRIDAY 7', which is wrong on every other day. The Dash to Panel dock has no running or focused-window indicators, so the user can't tell which apps are open.
