findings.fix: Show a live date on the calendar icon. Add a small teal pip under running apps and a stronger one for the focused app. Increase the icon size slightly.

findings.location: Top bar at the smaller scale
findings.problem: At 100% the bar and dock shrink, but the Vitals text is about 11px and its icons crowd the values. The bar is also visibly thinner than at 200%, so the proportions aren't scale-stable.
findings.fix: Set the bar height, font size and icon size in scale-independent units. Keep a minimum 13px text size and the icon gaps used at 200%.

pairs.reason: The Vitals readings have a consistent gap between each glyph and its value ("38%", "0.9", "13 B/s"), and date and time sit together as one unit. In a, the values are glued to their icons and the gap between date and time is too wide, so the bar reads as one run of characters.

In light mode the room keeps its teal strokes, so the brand mark survives the switch. In b it turns neutral grey and light mode loses CONSTRUCT's identity. a also keeps the icon-to-value spacing in the Vitals readings.
The Vitals glyphs and values have consistent spacing ("58%", "0.2"). In b they collide ("61%", "0.4" pressed against the icons), which hurts at-a-glance reading at small scale.
The overview chrome, search field and workspace card are identical. The only difference is the frozen harness readings, which aren't a product defect.
The top-bar readings keep their icon-to-value spacing. In b the glyphs and numbers run together. The app grid itself is the same apart from one extra app.

Toggles that are on use a solid teal fill with white labels, so they read clearly as on. In a the labels are teal on a dark-teal fill, which lowers contrast and makes Wired and Dark Style harder to tell apart from the toggles that are off.

Today is marked with a quiet tinted disc in the brand teal, which fits the calm-at-rest brief. a uses a saturated electric cyan, the loudest element on screen and a different hue from the wallpaper's teal.
b is broken: two notifications are drawn on top of each other in the same row ("Connected" and "Disk almost full" overlap), so neither can be read. In a the notification renders cleanly.
The clock and date sit at the optical centre, so the screen is balanced. In a the block is pushed into the top third, leaving the lower 60% as an orphaned empty field with no prompt or hint.
The unlock prompts are pixel-identical.

findings.location: Notification list, first row of the calendar/message tray
findings.problem: Two notifications ("Connected" and "Disk almost full") are drawn in the same slot. Titles, bodies, app headers and the close and expand buttons overlap and can't be read, and the disk warning, the one that matters, is lost.
findings.fix: Lay out stacked or grouped notifications as separate rows with their own height (or as a collapsed group with a count badge). Never paint a second item into the first item's allocation.

findings.location: Top-left banner "System · Backup finished", partly behind the open calendar menu
findings.problem: A transient banner shows while the message tray is open. It is cut off by the menu ("312 files were copied t…") and duplicates content that belongs in the list.
findings.fix: Hide or route banners into the tray list while the date menu is open. If one must show, place it fully clear of the open menu, never under it.

findings.problem: In light mode the wireframe room turns neutral grey, so the light variant loses the teal brand mark that defines CONSTRUCT.
findings.fix: Keep the teal strokes in light mode, darkened to meet 3:1 against the light background (as s02-a does), with the inner grid as a lighter tint of the same teal.

findings.location: Top bar, Vitals readings (memory, load, network)
findings.problem: The value text sits directly against its glyph ("45%", "0.8"), while other captures put a gap there. Spacing isn't defined in one place, so the readings run together and stop scanning as three separate measures.
findings.fix: Set one fixed gap between each Vitals glyph and its value (about 4px at 1x), a larger gap between readings (about 12px), and tabular figures so widths don't shift.

findings.location: Top bar, clipboard and tiling-layout indicators between Vitals and the system tray
findings.problem: The clipboard and layout icons swap order between the light and dark captures. The two extension icons also use different glyph weights and fills (a solid tile next to an outlined clipboard).
findings.fix: Pin a fixed order for extension indicators and redraw both glyphs at the same stroke weight as the system tray icons.

findings.problem: Today is a filled electric-cyan disc, a brighter hue than the brand teal used on the wallpaper and toggles. It is the loudest pixel on screen, against the calm-at-rest brief.
findings.fix: Use the accent teal at reduced opacity as the disc with bold teal numerals (as s07-b does), or a 2px teal ring. Reserve saturated cyan for focus rings only.

findings.location: Quick settings, on-state toggles (Wired, Dark Style)
findings.problem: Teal label and icon on a dark-teal fill give low contrast, and the on state isn't clearly distinct from the grey off tiles.
findings.fix: Fill on-state tiles with solid accent teal and white labels and icons (as s06-b does). Give the Wired split-arrow segment its own slightly darker teal so it reads as a separate target.

findings.problem: Two different apps share the identical teal room icon, and both labels truncate ("Install Con…", "Google Chr…"), so users can't tell the installer from the app.
findings.fix: Add a download badge or arrow to the installer's icon (or hide the installer once the system is installed). Allow two-line labels in the grid so names aren't cut off.

findings.location: Dock, the Calendar icon (white page with a red "FRIDAY") and the VS Code and terminal icons
findings.problem: The dock mixes the Tela-fork teal glyphs (Files, browser, Store) with a stock white-and-red calendar and saturated blue third-party icons. The calendar also shows "7" while the clock shows another date.
findings.fix: Supply Tela-fork versions in the teal/slate palette for the default dock apps (calendar and terminal at least), and make sure the calendar icon renders the live date.

findings.location: Notification column of the date menu, empty state
findings.problem: About 420px of panel width holds only a bell and "No Notifications". "Clear" stays visible but greyed out at very low contrast, as a dead control.
findings.fix: Hide "Clear" when the list is empty and shrink the empty column (or let the calendar take the full menu width when there are no notifications).

findings.problem: The clock and date sit in the top third with nothing below. There is no hint for how to unlock, so the lower two-thirds is an orphaned void and the next action isn't discoverable.
findings.fix: Centre the time block optically, as in s09-b, and add a quiet "Press any key or click to unlock" line, or the user's avatar and name near the bottom as in the macOS reference.

findings.location: Unlock prompt, password field and submit arrow
findings.problem: The submit chevron is oversized and grey and floats outside any button shape. The caret butts right against the first bullet, and the generic avatar with "Live session" carries no brand.
findings.fix: Put the chevron in a 32px circular teal button inside the field's right padding, add 4px between the caret and the bullets, and use a branded default avatar (the room glyph) for the live session.

findings.problem: The network icon reads as an empty monitor rectangle and the keyboard/accessibility glyph as a boxed square. At this size they are ambiguous and their weights don't match the volume and power glyphs.
findings.fix: Use clear wired-network and accessibility symbols from the same icon set at the same stroke weight, with the same spacing as the top bar's tray.

pairs.reason: The app content, layout, and visual treatment are indistinguishable; the top-bar readings are harness data.
Both versions present the same clear network hierarchy and controls.
The plain add affordance is quieter and better aligned with the restrained technical character than the isolated circular button.
The preference dialog’s content, contrast, and layout are effectively identical.
The teal room mark preserves the product’s distinctive identity in light mode, where b makes it recede into a generic gray background.
The terminal layouts are visually identical.
Its restrained cool palette keeps the monitoring view calmer and more coherent with the desktop theme.
The installer empty state, visual hierarchy, and window treatment are the same.
The security-keys screen is visually identical in both versions.

findings.problem: The final row of theme previews is visibly clipped by the modal boundary, obscuring available choices.
findings.fix: Make the preview area scrollable or resize the dialog/grid so every option is fully visible.

findings.problem: “Mouse & Touchpad” is cut off at the window edge with no visible scrolling affordance.
findings.fix: Use a clearly scrollable sidebar and reserve enough bottom padding to show the final navigation item.

findings.problem: The Wired add action alone uses a large outlined circular button while VPN uses a plain plus, creating inconsistent affordance weight for equivalent actions.
findings.fix: Standardize both section actions on the same compact plus-button treatment.

findings.location: Resources view, CPU, memory, network, and disk indicators
findings.problem: Unrelated saturated red, orange, yellow, green, and blue signals compete for attention even when the values are not warnings.
findings.fix: Use the restrained neutral/teal palette for normal telemetry; reserve warm colors for alert thresholds.

findings.problem: A very large terminal window contains only one prompt, producing excessive empty space for the primary developer workflow.
findings.fix: Adopt a more compact default terminal size or restore a useful working size based on prior session state.

findings.location: Light desktop wallpaper behind the modal
findings.problem: The wireframe room becomes low-contrast gray and loses its role as the recognizable brand cue.
findings.fix: Retain a muted teal treatment with sufficient contrast in light mode.

pairs.reason: Identical Files window; only the harness-driven top bar readings differ.
Same Settings Network page in both; only the Vitals values and dates differ.
Both show the same circled + on Wired, and nothing else differs.
The dark Preferences dialogs are identical apart from the Vitals text.
In the light room the wireframe stays teal, which matches the brand. In b it goes grey and the brand mark disappears.
The terminal windows are identical; only the harness values differ.
The System Monitor graphs and legend use a teal, blue and violet palette that fits the theme. In a the CPU series are raw red, orange, yellow and green, and read as alarm colours.
The Install window is the same in both; only the top bar numbers differ.
The top bar order is stable. In a the clipboard indicator jumps in front of the Vitals, and that shifts the layout.

findings.location: CPU legend, graph lines and Memory/Swap gauges
findings.problem: The stock red, orange, yellow and green series ignore the theme. Red reads as an error state next to a harmless 8% CPU reading.
findings.fix: Use a chart palette derived from the accent (teal, blue, violet, slate) for every series, and keep red for real errors.

findings.problem: The tick labels (50 secs, 100 %) are tiny and low-contrast against the dense grid lines.
findings.fix: Raise the axis label size and contrast, and fade the grid lines.

findings.problem: The clipboard indicator jumps from the right group to just after the clock, so the Vitals shift position between captures.
findings.fix: Pin the indicator order so the status area never reflows.

findings.problem: A long paragraph in tiny, low-contrast grey text runs about 90 characters per line. It is the key explanation for an important security feature.
findings.fix: Use body size with higher contrast, cap the line at 60-70 characters, and split it into short sentences.

findings.problem: The window sits in a 640px frame with a large empty area. The sidebar has no icon-size or section hierarchy, and the toggle is nearly invisible in its off state.
findings.fix: Make the off toggle track more visible, and give the empty state a clear primary action (Add a key as an accent button).

findings.location: Settings Network, + button next to Wired
findings.problem: Only the Wired + shows a ring, while the VPN + is bare. Equivalent controls look different.
findings.fix: Show the focus and hover ring only on interaction, and style all header + buttons the same.

findings.problem: The sidebar list is cut off mid-item at the bottom (Mouse & Touchpad), with no scroll affordance.
findings.fix: Add a fade or scrollbar, or make the window taller.

findings.problem: The light room is a flat pale grey-blue with a grey wireframe. The dark top bar and dock work against it, and the brand disappears.
findings.fix: Keep the teal wireframe on light and tint the surface with the accent.

findings.location: Preferences dialog over the dimmed parent window
findings.problem: The parent window's titlebar text is clipped and half-visible behind the modal (Ope…). The theme thumbnails scroll off the bottom edge.
findings.fix: Size the dialog to fit its content, or fade the clipped area.

findings.problem: The Projects folder has no glyph, unlike its siblings. The Desktop folder is a different, paler style. About half the window is empty.
findings.fix: Add a developer-folder glyph for Projects and unify the Desktop icon with the rest.

findings.problem: The terminal is a bare prompt, and the cursor and prompt have no accent. The empty window gives no hint of the brand.
findings.fix: Ship a themed prompt with a teal cursor and a CONSTRUCT palette.

findings.problem: The message 'no disk Construct can be installed on' is a dead end with no action and no explanation. The grey logo is large and stays inert.
findings.fix: Add a next step such as Continue in live mode, or Learn how, and tone down the logo.

findings.problem: The app icons mix flat teal tiles with full-colour third-party icons (VS Code blue, terminal blue). The calendar icon shows a static 'Friday 7'.
findings.fix: Recolour or theme the third-party icons with the Tela fork, and make the calendar icon dynamic.

pairs.reason: The Files windows are pixel-identical. Only the harness-frozen Vitals readings and the date differ.
The Settings › Network screens are identical apart from the frozen top-bar readings.
Both show the same hover ring on the Wired '+' and are otherwise identical.
The Text Editor Preferences dialogs in dark mode are identical apart from the frozen Vitals readings.

In light mode, version a draws the wireframe-room stroke behind the dialog in the teal accent. Version b draws it in neutral grey. Teal keeps the brand's one recognisable mark in the light theme, where it otherwise disappears.
The Terminal windows are identical.

Version a draws the CPU, memory, network and disk series in red, orange, yellow and green, so CPU1 at 13% looks like an alarm and status colours are used as decoration. Version b uses a calm teal, blue and violet series palette that leaves red and orange free for real warnings.
The Welcome empty states are identical.

Version a puts the clipboard indicator between the clock and the Vitals readings, so the top bar's status items are in a different order than on every other screen. Version b keeps the standard order: date, Vitals, then tray icons.

findings.location: Resources tab, CPU legend swatches, the memory pie and the network/disk arrows
findings.problem: The chart series use red, orange, yellow and green, the same hues the system uses for error, warning and success. CPU1 at 13% shows a red swatch and the memory pie is red at 52%, so normal load looks like a fault and the screen is loud at rest.
findings.fix: Ship the brand chart-series palette (teal, blue, violet, slate, as in s07-b) as the default in the System Monitor fork. Keep red and orange for threshold states only.

findings.location: Graph axis labels ('1 min', '50 secs', '100 %', '512 bytes/s') under and to the right of each graph
findings.problem: The axis labels are about 8px at 1x scale, so they are illegible on HiDPI even at 200%. The section headers (CPU, Memory and Swap, Network, Disk) sit directly under the previous section's legend with no gap, so the sections run together.
findings.fix: Raise the axis labels to the caption size (11px) in the dim foreground colour. Add about 16px above each expander header so each graph block is a distinct group.

findings.location: Swap and Memory rows: the pie icons beside the values
findings.problem: The pies are 16px and their value text is not aligned with the CPU legend grid. Swap's value sits one line lower than Memory's first line.
findings.fix: Align the Memory and Swap blocks to the same baseline as the CPU legend columns, and use the same swatch shape as the CPU legend instead of mini pies.

findings.problem: The last visible row is cut by the window edge without any fade or scroll affordance. The default window height crops the category list mid-row.
findings.fix: Increase the default height so it ends on a group divider, or add the libadwaita scroll-edge shadow at the bottom of the sidebar.

findings.location: Network page, the '+' buttons beside 'Wired' and 'VPN'
findings.problem: Wired's '+' shows a ringed circular button and VPN's '+' is a bare glyph. Two identical actions look different, and the ring reads as a stuck focus or hover state.
findings.fix: Give flat header-suffix buttons the same resting style. Show the circle only on hover and keyboard focus, using the accent focus ring.

findings.location: VPN group: the 'Not set up' card
findings.problem: The empty state is a full-height, centred placeholder card that is taller than a real row. It has the same border as the actionable rows, so it looks clickable but does nothing.
findings.fix: Render it as a standard row with dim left-aligned text, or put an 'Add VPN…' action row inside the card so the empty state leads to the action.

findings.location: 'Security keys' description paragraph under the heading
findings.problem: Three lines of small, low-contrast grey text (about 3.5:1) carry the most important explanation on the page. It runs to about 95 characters per line and is visually weaker than the 'No key added yet' row below it.
findings.fix: Use the body size with the standard dim-label opacity (at least 4.5:1). Cut the paragraph to two sentences and move the backup-key advice into the empty-state row.

findings.location: 'Lock the screen when a key is unplugged' switch (right)
findings.problem: The off-state switch track is nearly the same value as the row background, so the control almost disappears. The row also uses a filled background while the card above uses an outlined border: two card styles on one page.
findings.fix: Raise the off-state track contrast (e.g. 20% foreground on the card). Use one boxed-list style, outlined or filled, for both groups.

findings.location: Behind the Preferences dialog: the parent Text Editor header bar ('Ope…', 'New Document')
findings.problem: The modal is only about 20px narrower than the parent and sits 20px below its top, so the parent's header controls and title stick out above it as clipped text and half icons, which looks broken.
findings.fix: Dim the parent with the standard modal scrim, or attach the dialog at the parent's header (or centre it) so no truncated parent chrome shows around the dialog's edges.

findings.location: Style-scheme grid at the bottom of the Preferences dialog

Both calendars are the same except the empty-state bell and the today highlight. a's smaller bell is calmer. b's today marker is more legible and consistent with s06-b. Neither clearly wins.
b has a rendering bug: the "Disk almost full" notification overlaps the "Connected" one, with doubled headers and unreadable text. a renders cleanly.

The two screens are identical.

findings.location: Notification stack in the calendar popover, top-left
findings.problem: A second notification ("Disk almost full") renders on top of "Connected" with no clipping or animation settling. The headers and bodies overlap and cannot be read. This is also the only warning-class message, and it is lost.
findings.fix: Fix the notification-stack layout and transition so only one banner shows at a time. Give the warning its own state, using the restrained amber or red semantic colour with a clear icon.

findings.location: Floating "Backup finished" toast, top-left of the popover
findings.problem: The toast is cut off by the calendar popover ("copied t…"). It is too close to the popover and has no relationship to the popover edge.
findings.fix: Anchor toasts to the top-centre or the right edge, clear of the popover, or hide the toast while the popover is open.

findings.location: Top bar Vitals cluster (RAM, CPU, network)
findings.problem: In some captures (s01-b, s03-b) the icon-to-value gap collapses, and the numbers' widths shift between captures. The cluster reads as dense and jittery.
findings.fix: Use tabular figures and a fixed minimum width per reading. Set a constant icon-to-value gap of about 4px, and use the same gap at every scale.

findings.problem: The bar and dock stay as dark slabs on a pale grey desktop, and the grey wireframe has weak contrast. The light mode looks like a recolour of the dark theme, not a designed variant.
findings.fix: Use a light, translucent bar and dock in light mode. Keep the teal wireframe at tier-C contrast, and use a deliberate light wallpaper.

findings.problem: Active-state styling differs between the quick settings (teal fill or tint) and the calendar (today disc). Inactive tiles are low contrast, and the Power Mode tile is grey like the inactive ones, so its state is unclear.
findings.fix: Define a single "on" token (dark teal fill, cyan text and icon) and use it for every toggle, selection and today marker. Make inactive tiles clearly distinct from active ones.

findings.problem: The empty state is a large bell with a bold "No Notifications" label, which is more visual weight than a calm resting state needs. The "Clear" button is almost invisible.
findings.fix: Use a smaller, dimmer bell and lighter-weight text. Show "Clear" only when notifications exist.

findings.problem: The grid leaks adjacent-month days with the same weight as current-month days. Zero-padded dates and wide tracking read as odd.
findings.fix: Dim the days outside the current month. Remove the zero-padding on single-digit dates and tighten the tracking.

findings.location: App grid, Construct and Install CONSTRUCT icons
findings.problem: A version without the distinguishing arrow gives two near-identical icons. Truncated labels ("Google Chr...", "Install Con...") hide the difference.
findings.fix: Keep the arrow badge on the installer icon and shorten its label ("Install").

findings.problem: The lock screen is almost empty. There is no brand mark (the wireframe room), no wallpaper presence and no unlock hint, and the date is small against a very large clock.
findings.fix: Add a faint wireframe backdrop or logo and a subtle "Press any key" hint, and scale the date up slightly.

findings.problem: The field shows a generic user glyph with the label "Live session", and the submit chevron is oversized. The cyan focus ring is brighter than the rest of the UI.
findings.fix: Use a CONSTRUCT-styled avatar, a smaller chevron and a softer teal focus ring.

findings.problem: The dock carries the Calendar icon showing a static "FRIDAY 7" while the bar date differs, and it has no running-app indicators. The coloured third-party icons (VS Code blue, Ptyxis) clash with the monochrome teal set.
findings.fix: Show the live date on the icon and add running-app dots. Tint or normalise third-party icons toward the teal palette.

pairs.reason: The Vitals readings in the top bar have a real gap between each glyph and its value ("48%", "2.6"). In b the glyphs touch the numbers, so the three readings blur into one strip next to the clock.
In light mode b keeps the wireframe room in the teal accent. a turns it a neutral grey, which drops the one brand element from the most visible surface.
At 100% scale a keeps the space between glyph and value in the Vitals readings. b's tight version is hard to read at small size, which is the display-scale case being tested.
b uses the same evenly spaced glyph-then-value rhythm in the top bar as the other screens. a packs the glyphs against their values, so the overview's top bar reads differently from the desktop's.
In b, Install Construct uses the mark with a down arrow, so it can be told apart from the Construct app. In a the two tiles share the same icon and are only told apart by a truncated label.
The active toggles (Wired, Dark Style) use white labels on solid teal, which reads clearly as on. b's cyan text on dark teal is lower contrast and looks closer to the off tiles.

The empty state is scaled down to a quiet glyph and today's date is a solid teal disc with white numerals, the same on-state as quick settings. b's large grey bell is the loudest thing in the menu when there is nothing to report.
b is broken: two notifications (Connected and Disk almost full) are drawn on top of each other in the stack, so both headers, titles and bodies are unreadable. a shows a clean single notification.

The clock sits in the upper third, like the macOS reference, which leaves room for the unlock prompt that appears lower down. b centres it, so the clock and the avatar/password field fight for the same spot.
The two versions look identical.

findings.location: Calendar menu, notification list, top-left card
findings.problem: Two notifications are drawn in the same place. The 'Connected' and 'Disk almost full' headers, titles and bodies overlap, and the expand and close buttons collide. The list does not stack its entries.
findings.fix: Lay out each notification as its own row in a vertical list with a fixed gap, or collapse same-app notifications into one expandable group. Never place them on top of each other.

findings.location: Floating 'Backup finished' banner at top-centre, left of the calendar menu
findings.problem: The banner sits behind the open calendar menu and its body is cut off ('312 files were copied t'). While the menu is open, new banners collide with it.
findings.fix: Hide banners while the date menu is open, since they already appear in its list, or move them below the menu's left edge so neither covers the other.

findings.location: App grid, second row: 'Construct' and 'Install Con...' tiles
findings.problem: Two different actions, opening the app and installing the image, use the same teal room-mark tile. The only difference is a label truncated with an ellipsis.
findings.fix: Use the installer's own tile (the mark set back, with a down arrow, as in s05-b) wherever the installer appears. Rename it to something that fits, e.g. 'Install', so the label isn't truncated.

findings.location: Workspace thumbnails above the app grid
findings.problem: The two workspace previews differ in size and top edge (the left is larger and taller than the right), so the row looks misaligned.
findings.fix: Give every thumbnail the same size, top-aligned, with the active one marked by an outline in the accent colour rather than by size.

findings.location: Top bar, Vitals cluster (CPU, load, network)
findings.problem: Spacing between glyph and value changes from capture to capture: in some the glyph touches its number ('45%', '0.8'), in others there is a 4px gap. The clipboard and tiling icons that follow use a different gap again, so the right side of the bar has no consistent rhythm.
findings.fix: Use one token for the gap between glyph and value (about 4px) and one for the gap between items (about 12px). Apply them to Vitals, the clipboard and layout icons, and the system tray, and use tabular figures so values don't shift as they change.

findings.problem: The wireframe room turns neutral grey in light mode. The brand drops out entirely, and light and dark no longer read as the same product.
findings.fix: Keep the room's lines in a darker teal for light mode (as in s02-b), with the front edges at full strength and the grid lines tinted lighter.

findings.location: Top bar and dock in light mode
findings.problem: On a light desktop the top bar and dock stay near-black. Two heavy dark bands bracket the pale workspace, and the bar and dock do not follow the colour scheme.
findings.fix: In light mode, give the bar and dock a light surface with dark glyphs, or make the dark bar a deliberate choice for both schemes and soften it with a translucent tint over the wallpaper.

findings.location: Quick settings active toggles; today's date in the calendar
findings.problem: On-state is shown as cyan text and icons on a dark teal fill. The contrast is weak, and 'on' looks nearly the same as 'off' at a glance.
findings.fix: Use one on-state token across the system: solid accent fill with white or near-white label and icon (as in s06-a and s07-a). Apply it to toggles, today's date and selected items alike.

findings.location: Calendar menu, left pane empty state
findings.problem: An oversized grey bell outline (about 64px) is the heaviest thing in the menu even though it represents nothing. It draws attention away from the date and calendar.
findings.fix: Shrink the empty-state glyph to about 32px at reduced opacity, keep the 'No Notifications' label, and centre them optically in the pane.

findings.location: Calendar menu, 'Clear' button at bottom left
findings.problem: The disabled 'Clear' label is very low-contrast grey floating on its own in a large empty pane, with no button shape. It is hard to tell whether it is disabled or just faint.
findings.fix: Hide 'Clear' when the list is empty. When enabled, give it a button background and align it to the same bottom baseline as 'Select Weather Location…'.

findings.problem: The calendar icon is a white, light-skinned tile with a red 'FRIDAY' header and a static '7'. It clashes with the teal-and-dark palette and shows the wrong date next to the clock.
findings.fix: Redraw the calendar icon in the theme's palette (dark tile, teal header), and either show the current date dynamically or drop the number.

findings.problem: The radial glow behind the clock shows as a blotchy, square-ish halo with visible stepping on a dark field. It reads as a rendering artefact rather than as atmosphere.
findings.fix: Use a soft, large-radius, dithered gradient, or show a blurred, dimmed copy of the wireframe room so the lock screen carries the brand.

findings.problem: The submit chevron is a large grey glyph that crowds the reveal (eye) icon. The 2px bright-cyan focus ring is the loudest element on a screen meant to feel calm.
findings.fix: Make the submit button a round accent-filled button about the height of the field, and drop the focus ring to 1px of accent at reduced alpha or a soft inner glow.

findings.problem: Only network, volume, an unclear boxed glyph and power are shown. There is no battery level on a laptop-first product, and the boxed icon has no obvious meaning.
findings.fix: Add battery percentage to the lock screen's status area and replace the boxed glyph with a recognisable icon, or remove it.

pairs.reason: The sidebar’s selected row aligns with the toolbar icon rhythm instead of introducing an unnecessary second inset.
The application UI is visually the same; only harness-frozen top-bar readings and capture time differ.
Using the same plain add affordance for Wired and VPN is more internally consistent.
The preference dialog is visually the same; the clock difference is not product UI.
The teal wireframe wallpaper detail preserves CONSTRUCT’s brand cue in light mode.
The terminal UI is visually the same; only top-bar capture values differ.
The conventional, high-separation resource colors make CPU, network, and disk signals easier to scan.
It explains the recovery path and provides a clear “Look Again” action instead of leaving the user at a dead end.
Removing the duplicate body heading brings the explanatory content and key-management control higher into the reading order.

findings.problem: “Mouse & Touchpad” is visibly cut off by the window edge, with no scrollbar or continuation cue.
findings.fix: Make the navigation list independently scrollable and expose a scrollbar or fade/overflow cue when categories exceed the viewport.

findings.location: Preferences dialog, theme grid bottom edge
findings.problem: The theme choices are clipped beneath the modal boundary, so the available options and how to reach them are unclear.
findings.fix: Constrain the grid in a clearly scrollable content area, with visible scroll affordance and bottom padding.

findings.problem: The default window devotes nearly all of a large developer-facing terminal to empty space while the usable text area begins without contextual onboarding or status.
findings.fix: Use a more compact default terminal geometry or restore the last working size; preserve the spacious layout only after explicit resize.

findings.problem: The Wired add control has a circular button treatment while the equivalent VPN control is a bare plus, making equivalent actions appear to have different importance.
findings.fix: Use one add-control component and reserve circular treatment for a documented hover, focus, or primary-action state.

findings.problem: Resource colors change semantic meaning between CPU, memory, network, and disk areas, and several traces are too subtle against the grid.
findings.fix: Define a stable telemetry palette with adequate contrast and assign colors by metric role consistently across views.

findings.problem: The no-disk state gives no visible recovery action, even though the condition may change after a disk is connected.
findings.fix: Provide a primary rescan action such as “Look Again,” alongside concise guidance for the next step.

findings.problem: The body repeats the page title immediately below the centered title-bar title, consuming attention without adding context.
findings.fix: Remove the duplicate body heading and move the explanatory copy up, as in the stronger alternate layout.

pairs.reason: In a the sidebar selection pill spans the full sidebar width, as in Settings (c10). In b the pill is inset 24px on the left only, so it is lopsided and its icon is out of line with the header search icon.
The two are visually identical apart from the harness-driven Vitals and date.
Both show the same circled '+' state on Wired, and VPN's '+' is not circled. The difference is only in the top bar.
The Preferences dialog is identical in both. It sits on top of the parent window with its headerbar text bleeding through.
In light mode b's wallpaper wireframe stroke is teal, which keeps the brand. a's is grey-teal. The rest is identical, so the margin is small.
The terminal is identical in both.
b's chart series use the brand-derived hues, teal, mauve, violet and olive. a's red, orange, yellow and green read as alarm states, and red on idle memory suggests a fault that is not there.
a explains why the install can't proceed and gives a primary 'Look Again' action. b is a dead end with one terse line and a large empty lower half.

b's intro text is larger and higher contrast, and the off toggle is visible. a's three lines of dim, tiny grey text sit under a redundant duplicate heading, and its off toggle nearly vanishes into the row.

findings.location: Preferences dialog over the editor window
findings.problem: The dialog is laid over its parent, and the parent's headerbar text ('Ope…', 'New Document' and the icons) shows through and is clipped at the dialog's top edge. The theme preview list is also cut off mid-row at the bottom. It reads as a rendering fault.
findings.fix: Dim the parent window fully behind a modal and hide its headerbar content. Size the dialog to fit its content, or give the preview grid a visible scroll affordance, such as a fade or a scrollbar.

findings.location: Wallpaper wireframe fragment behind the dialog, around x=930, y=165
findings.problem: A stray teal wireframe corner pokes out above the window as a floating fragment. It looks like an artifact, not part of the room.
findings.fix: Dim the wallpaper or keep the room's lines clear of the window's centre. Otherwise let the wireframe carry the composition on the desktop.

findings.location: Terminal window, empty body and top bar
findings.problem: The terminal window floats mid-screen with the CONSTRUCT wireframe wallpaper nearly invisible behind it, and its prompt is a plain 'bash-5.3$'. The screen has little to say about the product beyond the generic GNOME Terminal, and the selected Terminal dock icon is a stock blue tile.
findings.fix: Ship a branded terminal profile: the teal accent for the cursor and prompt, and a CONSTRUCT-coloured dock icon for the app. Make the room wallpaper readable at rest.

findings.problem: The last visible row is cut by the window's bottom edge with no scroll cue. The sidebar has about 13 entries and the window is short.
findings.fix: Open Settings taller by default, or add an edge fade or scrollbar to the sidebar so the cut-off reads as scrolling.

findings.location: Wired row: toggle and gear, and Wired/VPN '+' buttons
findings.problem: The Wired row says only 'Connected' with no interface name, IP or speed. A developer cannot read the network's state at a glance. The '+' buttons are bare glyphs, and one of them shows a circular hover ring that the other does not, so it is unclear whether they are controls.
findings.fix: Show interface, IP and link speed as a secondary line. Give every section '+' a consistent resting affordance, such as a subtle circular button.

findings.problem: The window controls sit on the content pane, but the sidebar title 'Settings' is small and the controls are low contrast.
findings.fix: Raise the contrast of the minimise, maximise and close glyphs to match the title text.

findings.problem: The top bar crowds about 10 items into the right side, with an undifferentiated cluster of small tray glyphs: clipboard, layout, display, volume, lock and power. The Vitals glyphs (battery, CPU, network) and their values are tiny, close together and equal in weight to the clock.
findings.fix: Group the Vitals and the system tray with visible dividers or extra spacing. Use a tabular figure style so the values do not shift the clock. Keep the clock the most prominent item.

findings.problem: Running apps are marked only by a very small dot under the icon and a faint tile behind it. The active app and the other running apps are hard to tell apart, and the Settings icon is a blue circle that clashes with the teal icon set.
findings.fix: Make the active and running indicators larger and use the teal accent. Re-colour the Settings, Terminal and VS Code icons to the Tela-fork palette.

findings.location: Preferences dialog, large empty zone above the 'Appearance' title
findings.problem: There is about 40px of empty space between the headerbar and the 'Appearance' label. Above it there is no group title or spacing rhythm, and the label is bold white with no section hierarchy to the swatches below.
findings.fix: Tighten the top padding to one spacing step and treat 'Appearance' as a group title, using the same title style as other pages.

pairs.reason: In a, the Files sidebar's selected pill runs to the window edge with the icons inset, the same way the Settings sidebar does it. b indents the whole list, so its pill and icon column sit 12px off the Settings grid. Sidebars in two core apps then look different.
The two are pixel-identical except for the Vitals readings the harness freezes, which aren't a product difference.
Both show the same Network page, and both draw a circled hover/focus ring around Wired's + but not VPN's. Nothing separates them.
The Text Editor Preferences sheets are identical in dark mode. Only the frozen Vitals and the clock differ.
The light-mode Preferences sheets are identical, including the teal-outlined preview and the selected scheme card.
The terminal windows are identical. Only the top-bar readings differ.

In b the chart series use muted, evenly spaced hues built from the teal accent. a uses saturated red, orange, yellow and green, so CPU1 and Memory at 50% show in red, which reads as an alarm. That breaks the rule that status colours mean one thing, and it isn't calm at rest.
In a, the no-disk state explains what's wrong (only the boot stick is available) and gives a primary 'Look Again' action. b just states a fact and leaves the user with nothing to do.

b drops the 'Security keys' heading that a repeats right under the header bar. b's description is set at body size in readable contrast, where a's is small and low contrast. b's toggle knob is also visible, while in a it disappears into the track, so the off state can't be read.

findings.location: Network page, the '+' at the right of the Wired header
findings.problem: Wired's + shows a circular outlined button and VPN's + right below it is a bare glyph. Two identical actions look different (it's a hover/focus state with no keyboard context), and the ring is heavier than anything else on the page.
findings.fix: Make header-suffix flat buttons share one resting style. Show the hover state as a subtle filled circle (accent at 10% alpha), not an outline, and give the focus ring only on keyboard focus, using the teal accent focus colour.

findings.location: Construct app, content area under the 'Security keys' header bar
findings.problem: 'Security keys' appears twice, as the window title and as a page heading. The description under it is ~11px in a low-contrast grey, so the most important explanation on a security page is the hardest text to read.
findings.fix: Drop the in-page heading, or keep it only when the page has several groups. Set the description in the body style (same size as the row titles) using the dim-label colour at ≥4.5:1 contrast, as s09-b does.

findings.location: 'Lock the screen when a key is unplugged' row, the switch
findings.problem: The off switch's knob is nearly the same colour as its track, so the state can't be read and the control barely looks interactive.
findings.fix: Give the off knob a light neutral fill (the s09-b treatment) and keep track and knob at ≥3:1 non-text contrast in both dark and light.

findings.problem: The clipboard indicator sits between the clock and the Vitals here, but to the right of Vitals on every other capture. Indicator order shifts depending on load order.
findings.fix: Pin indicator order in the panel config (clock, Vitals, clipboard, layout, system) so the clipboard indicator's position doesn't depend on extension load order.

findings.location: Resources: CPU legend swatches, Memory pie, Disk/Network arrows
findings.problem: Series colours are the stock saturated red/orange/yellow/green. At 50% use, CPU1 and Memory show in red, and error and warning colours become data labels.
findings.fix: Keep the s07-b palette: series hues from the teal-based chart ramp, four hues apart, with red and amber reserved for thresholds.

findings.location: Memory and Swap row, Swap indicator; Network/Disk arrows
findings.problem: At 0%, the swap pie shrinks to a 6px violet dot that looks like a stray bullet. The mauve 'Sending' and 'Writing' arrows are muddy and close in value to the background.
findings.fix: Draw the pie's empty track ring (neutral 20%) so a 0% value still reads as a gauge. Lift the mauve's lightness to match the teal arrow's luminance.

findings.problem: Axis labels are ~8px at 1× and sit below a legible size on HiDPI. Unit spacing is inconsistent ('100 %' next to '1.0 KiB/s').
findings.fix: Set axis labels to the caption style (≥10px logical, tabular figures) and use one unit format throughout.

findings.problem: The no-disk state has no action and no next step, just a large icon and a single line over a lot of empty space.
findings.fix: Keep s08-a's two-sentence explanation and its primary 'Look Again' button. Also add a secondary 'Keep trying Construct' that closes the window.

findings.problem: The button is a saturated cyan fill with dark text, the brightest element on the screen, and it doesn't match the deeper teal of the dock's active tile and the selected sidebar row.
findings.fix: Make suggested-action buttons use the same teal accent token as the selection pills (the darker teal), with light text, so the accent comes from one source.

findings.location: Files sidebar, the list's left inset
findings.problem: The sidebar list is indented 12px more than in Settings and the Construct app, so the selected pill and icon column don't line up across the three sidebars.
findings.fix: Use one sidebar row metric for all apps: pill flush to the pane's leading edge, 12px icon inset, 8px gap to the label.

findings.location: Text Editor Preferences sheet over the main window
findings.problem: The sheet covers the parent's header bar, but parent fragments still show around its top edge ('Op…', a cut-off title, icons). Its scheme grid is cut off at the bottom with no scroll indicator. The wireframe wallpaper's line also pokes out above the window.
findings.fix: Dim the parent header under the sheet, or give the dialog a top margin that clears the parent header. Size the sheet to fit the full scheme grid, or show an overlay scrollbar and a bottom fade.

findings.problem: 'Mouse & Touchpad' is clipped at the window's bottom edge with no fade, so the list looks like it ends there.
findings.fix: Add a bottom scroll fade (undershoot) to sidebar lists, or set the default window height so the clip falls between rows.

findings.location: Network page, 'VPN — Not set up' row
findings.problem: The placeholder row is a full-size empty card with centred grey text. It weighs as much as the real Connected row and pads out the page.
findings.fix: Render empty groups as a compact dim-label line under the header, or merge the placeholder into the '+' (an 'Add VPN…' row).

findings.location: Terminal window, content area and header bar
findings.problem: The prompt is the default 'bash-5.3$' and nothing in the header bar signals CONSTRUCT. The terminal, the main surface for the audience, has the least identity of all the screens.
findings.fix: Ship a default prompt showing user@host and cwd in the accent colour, and a terminal palette from the same chart and brand ramp.

pairs.reason: The desktop compositions are visually identical; the differing system readings are harness data.

Both provide the same calm desktop layout at this scale.

The quick-settings panels are visually equivalent.

The login views are visually identical.

findings.problem: The next workspace card is clipped at the screen edge with no visible paging or navigation cue, making the workspace carousel’s extent ambiguous.
findings.fix: Show a deliberate partial-card affordance plus workspace paging/navigation, or fit complete workspace cards in the overview viewport.

findings.problem: The sparse grid leaves a large unused lower half of the screen while app targets are widely separated, reducing scanning efficiency for a developer-oriented launcher.
findings.fix: Use a denser adaptive grid or center the full grid vertically while preserving predictable row and column spacing.

findings.problem: The empty notifications state consumes most of a very large pane, while the actionable calendar and agenda controls are compressed into the right column.

findings.location: notification stack at top of panel

findings.problem: The field has no visible password label or placeholder, and the oversized chevron competes with the visibility control, weakening first-use clarity.

findings.problem: The three agenda/action rows share nearly identical muted treatment, making their different roles hard to scan.

a renders overlapping, unreadable notification text in the stack; b is clean and legible.

findings.location: Notification list in the date menu, top-left of the panel

findings.location: Toast 'Backup finished' at top-left, behind the date menu panel

findings.location: App grid, desktop thumbnails strip (two small boxes)

findings.location: Quick settings, tile labels and the slider
findings.problem: Toggle on-state colour is inconsistent: bright cyan text on dark teal against a fill. The volume slider has no value or mute state. Sub-labels such as 'Balanced' are small and low contrast.

findings.location: Date menu, calendar grid and event rows
findings.problem: Weekday letters and out-of-month days are very low contrast. 'Add World Clocks…' and 'Select Weather Location…' take space for features developers rarely use.

findings.location: Top bar Vitals readings at the right
findings.problem: Readings (RAM, CPU, network) have inconsistent gaps between icon and value, and no units or labels except the network rate. The bar's text is small beside the icons.
findings.fix: Apply a fixed gap between icon and value, add units, and use tabular figures so the layout doesn't shift.

findings.problem: The lock screen is a near-black void with a large clock. The wireframe room, the brand's key asset, is absent, and the status icons at top right have no labels.
findings.fix: Show a faint teal wireframe behind the clock. Add a hint such as 'Swipe or press a key to unlock'.

findings.location: Date menu on the desktop, left half
findings.problem: With no notifications the left half is a big empty area with a large grey bell, which is not calm at rest. The 'Clear' button is dim but still shown.
findings.fix: Shrink the bell, hide Clear when empty, and keep the panel compact.

findings.problem: The dock has no running-app indicators or active state. The Calendar icon is hardcoded to 'FRIDAY 7', which doesn't match the date.
findings.fix: Add dots under running apps and use a live calendar icon.

pairs.reason: The Vitals readings put a space between each glyph and its number ("46%", "2.3", "11 KB/s"), so the three metrics read as separate items. In a, the icons sit against the numbers and the cluster blurs together.
In light mode, b keeps the wireframe room in the brand teal. In a it goes grey, which loses the product's single identity element and makes the desktop look like an unthemed placeholder.
At the smaller scale, b keeps a gap between each Vitals icon and its value. In a the tight glyphs and numbers merge at that size.
The overview is otherwise identical. b's spaced Vitals readings are the only difference, and they scan better.
In b, 'Install Construct' gets its own tile (the mark with a down arrow). In a it uses the same icon as 'Construct', so the two can't be told apart in the grid.

In b, active toggles (Wired, Dark Style) are a solid teal fill with white labels, so on vs off is clear at a glance. In a, the cyan labels on a dim teal tint are low-contrast and look close to inactive.
In b the empty state is quieter (smaller bell, no dead 'Clear' button), and today in the calendar is a filled teal pill. It is calmer, and the one meaningful state is clearer.
In a, two notifications render on top of each other in the list ('System' twice, with overlapping titles and bodies), which is broken. b shows a single clean card.
In a the clock sits in the upper third, which matches GNOME and macOS and leaves room below for the unlock prompt. b centres the clock vertically, so it jumps when the password view opens.
The two unlock screens are pixel-identical.

findings.location: Notification list, top-left of the calendar popover
findings.problem: Two notifications ('Connected' and 'Disk almost full') are drawn in the same slot. Headers, titles and bodies overlap and can't be read, and the collapse chevron and close button are doubled.
findings.fix: Fix the message-list stacking so that grouped notifications either expand into separate rows or collapse into one card showing a '+1' count. Never overlay their text.

findings.location: Banner at top-centre, left of the popover
findings.problem: The 'Backup finished' banner shows while the calendar popover is open. The popover covers it and cuts the body off at 'copied t'.
findings.fix: Suppress or dismiss banners while the date menu is open, since the same message already appears in the list. Otherwise place banners so they never sit under the popover.

findings.location: Top bar and dock in light mode
findings.problem: In light mode the top bar and dock stay near-black on a pale desktop. This heavy dark frame breaks the calm-at-rest goal and doesn't follow the light scheme.
findings.fix: Give the panel and dock a light-surface variant (pale slate with dark glyphs), or a translucent tint of the desktop colour, in light mode.

findings.location: Top bar, right cluster: layout and clipboard icons
findings.problem: In light mode the window-layout and clipboard indicators are in the opposite order from dark mode (s01/s06), so the same controls move between schemes.
findings.fix: Pin the indicator order in the panel configuration, independent of colour scheme or extension load order.

findings.problem: The clock is vertically centred, and nothing tells the user how to unlock (no 'Press any key' or 'Click to unlock'). There is a large empty area below the date.
findings.fix: Keep the clock in the upper third (as in s09-a) and add a quiet hint line near the bottom, e.g. 'Type or click to unlock', in secondary text colour.

findings.problem: The submit chevron is oversized, grey and has no button shape. It is out of scale with the eye icon and runs into the field's cyan focus ring.
findings.fix: Render submit as a circular button the same height as the field, with a 16px chevron, teal when the field has text and dim when empty, separate from the input.

findings.location: App grid, 'Google Chr...' and 'Install Con...' labels
findings.problem: Labels are cut off at about 12 characters even though the grid has room. The installer, the main call to action on a live image, is the label that gets truncated.
findings.fix: Allow two-line labels in the app grid, or rename the desktop entries to 'Chrome' and 'Install'.

findings.problem: The calendar icon is a static 'FRIDAY 7' with a red header. It shows the wrong date and brings in a red that appears nowhere else in the palette.
findings.fix: Use a themed calendar glyph without a date, in the Tela-fork teal and slate, or a live icon that shows today's date.

findings.location: Top bar, right status icons (display, volume, square-with-lock, power)
findings.problem: The third glyph (a square with a small lock or box) can't be identified, and the display icon reads as a monitor rather than a wired network. Status meaning can't be read at a glance.
findings.fix: Use the standard network-wired and input-source symbolic icons from the Tela fork, and add tooltips to every indicator.

findings.problem: With no notifications, 'Clear' is still shown in disabled grey: a dead control in a calm state.
findings.fix: Hide 'Clear' when the list is empty, as s07-b already does.

findings.location: Quick Settings, active toggles 'Wired' and 'Dark Style'
findings.problem: Active state is cyan text on a dim teal tint, which is low contrast, and the 'Wired' label is barely set apart from inactive tiles.
findings.fix: Use a solid accent fill with white label and icon for active toggles (as in s06-b), and keep the tinted style for hover only.

pairs.reason: The selected sidebar state is anchored to the sidebar edge, making the navigation grouping and current location clearer.
The application UI is visually identical; only frozen top-bar telemetry differs.
Keeping both add controls visually equivalent avoids implying that the Wired action has a different interaction model.
The application UI is visually identical; only frozen top-bar telemetry differs.
The teal wireframe wallpaper remains perceptible behind the light modal, retaining the product’s identity across themes.
The terminal UI is visually identical; only frozen top-bar telemetry differs.
Its restrained resource-chart palette feels calmer and avoids making ordinary CPU activity read as warning status.
It explains the recovery path and provides an explicit “Look Again” action rather than leaving the user at a dead end.
The explanatory copy has materially better contrast and avoids repeating the page heading inside the content.

findings.problem: “Mouse & Touchpad” is visibly cut off at the bottom of the navigation with no evident scroll affordance.
findings.fix: Make the sidebar independently scrollable and preserve bottom padding or resize the window so complete rows are visible.

findings.problem: The theme-card grid is clipped by the modal’s lower boundary, with no visible scrollbar or indication that more choices exist.
findings.fix: Add a visible scrolling region or constrain the grid to complete rows with an explicit overflow affordance.

findings.location: Behind the Preferences modal, upper window chrome
findings.problem: The obscured parent title-bar labels remain legible enough to compete with the modal header.
findings.fix: Increase backdrop dimming/blur or use a more opaque modal backdrop so the dialog is unambiguously foregrounded.

findings.problem: The no-disk state has no visible recovery action, despite being a condition that can change after attaching storage.
findings.fix: Provide a primary “Look Again” action and concise guidance to attach a destination disk.

findings.location: Security keys content, beneath page title
findings.problem: The content repeats “Security keys” immediately below the identical window title, spending scarce vertical space without adding context.
findings.fix: Remove the duplicated in-content heading and begin with the explanatory text or a concise section label.

findings.problem: The muted description is substantially lower contrast than adjacent controls, weakening legibility for important security behavior.
findings.fix: Use the standard secondary-text color with sufficient contrast, matching the stronger treatment in s09-b.

findings.problem: Red, orange, and green are assigned to ordinary CPU series, making neutral identity colors resemble warning/success status colors.
findings.fix: Use a restrained categorical palette for series and reserve semantic red, amber, and green for actionable system states.

pairs.reason: The sidebar selection pill is inset from the window edge and lines up with the content. In b it runs flush to the window border, so it looks clipped.
The two Settings captures are visually identical. Only the harness-driven top bar values differ.
Both show the same circled + hover or focus state, and everything else is identical.
The Text Editor preferences are identical. Only the top bar readings differ.
The light-mode preferences are identical in layout and colour. Only the clock differs.
The terminal captures are identical apart from the harness-driven top bar values.

The chart series use a restrained teal, mauve, violet and olive palette that fits the brand. In b, red, orange, yellow, green and blue read as status colours, and red on CPU1 and Memory looks like an alarm.
It explains the situation and gives a clear next action (the Look Again button). In b the empty state is a dead end: one line and no action.
The description is larger, high-contrast and readable. In a it is tiny, dim grey text that is hard to read on the dark background. The toggle's off state is also clearer in b.

findings.location: Text Editor window behind the Preferences dialog
findings.problem: The Preferences dialog overlaps its parent window, which is visible behind it. The parent's title and headerbar controls are clipped and show through the dialog edge. A teal wallpaper fragment also pokes out above the window. The stacking looks broken.
findings.fix: Dim the parent window or inset it with a proper modal scrim. Centre the dialog over the parent with a consistent offset.

findings.problem: The 'Mouse & Touchpad' row is cut off at the window bottom, with no scroll cue.
findings.fix: Size the window so rows are not clipped mid-row, or add a fade or scroll affordance.

findings.problem: The terminal body is a flat slate with a single prompt. The window colour is lighter than the desktop with no teal accent. The terminal looks like a generic GNOME terminal, and the window and wallpaper do not feel part of the CONSTRUCT brand.
findings.fix: Use a deeper terminal background tied to the brand palette. Add a teal cursor and a themed prompt.

findings.problem: The 11px body copy is dim grey on near-black, below comfortable contrast. It is a long paragraph under a small heading.
findings.fix: Use the primary text colour at 13px or larger and shorten the line length.

findings.problem: In variant b the highlight pill is flush to the window edge with no margin, and icons are indented differently from the content below.
findings.fix: Inset the sidebar rows by about 8px so the pill sits inside the window.

findings.problem: The axis labels are tiny and the charts are mostly empty grids. Legend swatches are large relative to the data.
findings.fix: Raise the axis label size and reduce the legend swatch size.

pairs.reason: The selected-row pill in b sits flush to the sidebar edge with the icon column at the same inset as Settings and the Construct app. In a the pill floats 24px in, so the Files sidebar breaks the selection pattern used by the other sidebars.
The two captures are pixel-identical apart from the harness-frozen Vitals readings and the date.
The two captures are identical. Both show the same ring on the Wired '+' and none on the VPN '+'.
The Preferences dialog is identical in both. Only the top-bar readings differ.
In a, the wallpaper line visible above the dialog is drawn in the brand teal. In b it is a flat grey, so light mode loses the one trace of the wireframe-room identity on the screen.
The terminal window is identical in both. Only the top-bar readings differ.

a draws CPU/memory/disk series from a restrained palette anchored on the brand teal. b uses stock red/orange/yellow/green, so memory reads as an error in red and CPUs look like traffic-light status, which breaks the rule that status colours mean one thing.
a explains why there is no target disk, offers two ways forward and has a primary 'Look Again' action. b is a dead end with one sentence and nothing to do.

b drops the 'Security keys' heading that repeated the page title, sets the explanation at a readable size and contrast, and shows the off toggle's knob. In a the off switch is nearly invisible and the description is small, dim grey text.

findings.location: Network page, 'Wired' section header, '+' button at right
findings.problem: When the window opens, the Wired '+' button shows a filled circular ring while the identical VPN '+' does not. Initial keyboard focus is drawn as a visible focus ring on a destructive-free but arbitrary control, so the page is not calm at rest and two identical buttons look different.
findings.fix: Only show the focus ring when focus came from the keyboard (:focus-visible), or set the window's initial focus to the sidebar list so no header button carries a ring on open.

findings.location: 'Look Again' primary button vs. accent elsewhere (Files folder icons, sidebar selection text, toggles)
findings.problem: The accent comes in at least two hues: a near-neon cyan on buttons, toggles and selected text, and a deeper teal on folder icons, the dock tiles and the wallpaper line. The saturated cyan button is the loudest thing on the screen and clashes with the quiet teal brand.
findings.fix: Define one accent token in the brand teal plus one lighter tint for text on dark, and derive button fill, toggle, selected label and icon-theme folder colour from those two tokens.

findings.problem: The hero mark is a flat blue-grey with no teal, and it uses the plain mark rather than the installer's arrow-down tile that appears in the dock. The illustration and the app icon tell different stories.
findings.fix: Use the installer tile, the mark set back with an arrow down, as the hero, drawn in the accent teal on its line strokes.

findings.problem: Colour and direction are mapped inconsistently. In Network, teal is a down-arrow and means receive. In Disk, teal is an up-arrow and means read, while rose is up for sending but down for writing. One colour carries two directions within the same window.
findings.fix: Bind colour to direction: one hue for inbound (receive/read) and another for outbound (send/write), with the arrow pointing the same way in both sections.

findings.location: Graph axis labels ('100 %', '512 bytes/s', '1 min', '50 secs')
findings.problem: The axis labels render at about 8px logical size in light grey and crowd the plot's right edge ('512 bytes/s' nearly touches the window border). They are hard to read on a HiDPI laptop, while legend values are set at body size, so the hierarchy is inverted.
findings.fix: Raise axis labels to the caption size (11–12px), use tabular numerals, abbreviate units ('512 B/s', '60s'), and reserve a fixed gutter on the right for the y-axis.

findings.location: Preferences dialog over the Text Editor window, top edge and bottom edge
findings.problem: The parent window's header text ('Ope…', 'New Document', icons) shows through as a cut-off strip above the dialog. The dialog's scheme grid is cut mid-row at the bottom with no fade or scrollbar to hint that more content is below.
findings.fix: Dim the parent fully under the modal, or attach the dialog as a sheet below the parent's header bar. Add a bottom scroll shadow, or size the dialog so the grid ends on a full row.

findings.location: Markdown preview card border vs. selected scheme thumbnail
findings.problem: The non-interactive preview has a 2px bright-cyan border that reads as a focus or selection state. The actually selected scheme instead uses a white border with a cyan check, so selection looks two different ways and the eye goes to the wrong element.
findings.fix: Give the preview a neutral 1px border, and use one selection treatment (accent border plus check) for the chosen scheme.

findings.location: Security keys page, 'Lock the screen when a key is unplugged' switch (a)
findings.problem: Version a draws the off switch as a dark knob on a dark track, so it is nearly invisible and the control's affordance is lost. b fixes this, but the switch style still differs from the Settings switch in s02.
findings.fix: Use one switch token everywhere: a light-grey knob on a mid-grey track when off, and an accent track when on, the same as the Settings Network page.

findings.location: Top bar, clipboard icon between clock and Vitals (a)
findings.problem: In s09-a the clipboard indicator sits between the clock and the Vitals readings, while every other capture places it after Vitals. The order of top-bar items is not fixed, which hurts reading the system state at a glance.
findings.fix: Pin the top-bar indicator order in the extension configuration: clock, then Vitals, then the clipboard and layout indicators, then the system menu.

findings.problem: The Desktop folder is drawn as a light-teal screen glyph with a different silhouette and value from the other eight solid-teal folders, so it breaks the grid's rhythm.
findings.fix: Redraw Desktop in the Tela-fork folder template (same tab, same body tint) with a desktop emblem, like Documents and Downloads.

findings.location: Dock, terminal icon (4th) and VS Code icon
findings.problem: The terminal icon is a periwinkle/blue tile and VS Code is stock blue, while the rest of the dock is teal. The developer's most-used app is the one icon that is off-palette.
findings.fix: Re-tint the terminal icon in the icon-theme fork to the teal family (dark tile, teal prompt glyph) so the core dev tools share the brand palette.

findings.problem: The last sidebar row is cut flush by the window's bottom edge with no fade or scroll hint, so the sidebar looks complete and the remaining sections cannot be discovered.
findings.fix: Add a bottom scroll-edge shadow to sidebars, the same overflow treatment as the dialog fix above.

findings.location: Top bar and dock in light mode
findings.problem: In light mode, the windows and wallpaper turn pale while the top bar and dock stay near-black. This makes the heaviest contrast on screen at the edges and pulls attention away from the work area.
findings.fix: Either give the shell a light variant that follows the colour scheme, or soften the dark shell in light mode (lower opacity, lighter border) so it reads as a frame, not a band.
